### [SEQ:72] [Data Pad] [22:52:51]
============================================================

## DATA PAD: Research Log -- Rui Childs
**Found at:** Hollowpoint Relay | **Tone:** gaslighting | **Type:** research log

---

Day 47.

HERMES confirmed the temperature was stable. Her breath fogged. HERMES confirmed the temperature was stable.

The samples aren't behaving. That's not the right word. Samples don't behave. They exhibit properties. These are exhibiting properties outside any reference material available to me. the Bloom, or what the brief says is the Bloom, has a thermal signature that inverts at night. It shouldn't have a thermal signature at all.

Ran the spectrograph three times. Same result. The crystalline structure shifts at the molecular level when the temperature drops below -20C. Not fracturing. Reorganizing. Like it's adapting.

-- Rui Childs, Lab 2

---

Day 49.

Filed the anomaly report. Standard form. Ref AR-3608. Dr. Huang reviewed it, handed it back, and told me to rerun the tests. I reran them. Same results. They told me to rerun them again.

I understand now that the form isn't for reporting anomalies. The form is for making anomalies disappear.

Dev from Lab 2 transferred out. No notice. His workstation was cleared by 0600. The samples are still here. Nobody came for them. Nobody came for his things either.

---

Day 55.

He remembered the door being red. Everyone said it was always grey. The paint was grey.

I've stopped filing reports. I've started keeping this instead. The samples from Hollowpoint Relay are doing something at night that I can't explain with the equipment I've been given. So I requisitioned better equipment. Request denied. Budget code: INSUFFICIENT AUTHORIZATION.

I brought my personal spectrometer. The readings don't match the Mammona-issue unit. Not slightly off. Fundamentally different. Like the standard equipment is calibrated to miss what I'm finding.

That's not a malfunction. That's a decision someone made.

---

Day 63.

Tor Oduya approached me after shift. Said they saw my after-hours lab access in the logs. I expected a warning. Instead: "I've been seeing the same thing in warp key fragments. For months. My reports go nowhere too."

We compared data. The correlation is. I don't have a word for it. These aren't coincidences. There's a pattern. The pattern has intent.

I locked the data on a sealed drive. Personal encryption. If the standard equipment is lying to us, I don't trust the standard network either.

---

Day 81.

The report said clear. She'd measured the contamination herself. The report said clear.

Dr. Oduya didn't show up for shift. Transferred, they said. Same word they used for Dev. Same paperwork. Same empty workstation by morning.

I checked the sealed drive. The data I locked is still there. But there's a new file. I didn't create it. It's a personnel dossier. My personnel dossier. With a field I've never seen before: RETENTION STATUS. The value is PENDING.

---

Day 96.

I'm leaving this pad in Hollowpoint Relay. If you find it, the sealed drive is behind panel 19 in the maintenance crawlspace off Section E. The encryption key is my mother's maiden name. Mammona doesn't have it. They don't have my mother's maiden name either. At least I hope they don't.

-- Rui

[The final entry was written in a different ink. The handwriting deteriorates toward the end.]

---

**Cross-reference:** See historical record 'The Missing Report'

## DATA PAD: Maintenance Log -- Eunji Brennan
**Found at:** Voss Landing | **Tone:** claustrophobia | **Type:** maintenance log

---

**MAINTENANCE LOG -- Water Recycler Unit 3**
**Tech:** Eunji Brennan (EB-264)
**Date:** Day 5

Routine inspection. All parameters within spec. Filter replacement completed. Calibration nominal. Estimated next service: Day 35.

Notes: None. Clean run.

-- EB-264

---

**Date:** Day 14

Unscheduled check. Night shift reported a vibration in the walls near the assembly. Inspected. Couldn't reproduce. All readings nominal at time of inspection.

Action: monitoring. Will revisit next scheduled maintenance.

-- EB-264

---

**Date:** Day 28

The ceiling was 2.1 meters. Standard. It felt lower every day.

Follow-up on previous entry. The sound is still present. Louder. I isolated the section and disconnected non-essential components. Sound continued. It's not coming from the machine. It's coming through it.

Submitted work order for diagnostic overhaul. Status: queued. Estimated wait: 2 weeks.

Something isn't right. I don't have data to support that statement. After 15 years of fixing machines, you develop a feeling in your hands. The feeling says something isn't right.

-- EB-264

---

**Date:** Day 36

Diagnostic overhaul completed. 8 hours of testing. Every component individually verified. Every sensor calibrated. Every connection checked.

Result: the system is operating perfectly. Better than perfectly. Efficiency is up 7% from installation baseline. That shouldn't be possible on equipment this age with this service history.

But here's the thing that keeps me up: during the overhaul, I found a component I didn't install. Didn't order. Can't identify. It's wired into the main bus. It's functioning. I don't know what it does. I tried to remove it. It's grown into the surrounding wiring. 'Grown' is the word. I'm using it deliberately.

I'm filing this under 'resolved, nominal' because that's what the data says. The data is wrong. I don't know how to file that.

-- EB-264

---

**Date:** Day 59

The ventilation cut for thirty seconds. In the dark, the walls moved.

I found something behind the access panel that shouldn't be there. Not a component. A cavity. Small. The size of a fist. The interior surface is smooth in a way that machined metal isn't smooth. In a way that nothing manufactured is smooth. And there's something in it. Small. Warm. I didn't touch it.

I closed the panel. I'm not going to open it again.

I'm not going to file this.

-- EB-264

[No further entries in this log. Subsequent maintenance logs for Water Recycler Unit 3 are filed by a different technician. They describe the system as 'nominal.']

---

### [SEQ:85] [Data Pad] [22:52:52]
============================================================

## DATA PAD: Research Log -- Hanna Belov
**Found at:** Nemaea Surface | **Tone:** military | **Type:** research log

---

Day 97.

Contact, bearing 270, range 200 meters, count unknown. Weapons free.

The readings don't make sense. Not wrong. They make sense, just not in any framework I was trained in. Eldritch Nodes is producing output that the spectrometer interprets as noise. It isn't noise. Noise is random. This has structure. Mathematical structure. The kind that implies a system behind it.

I ran the analysis twice. Both times the software flagged the data as 'instrument error.' The instrument is fine. I calibrated it this morning. The data is accurate. The data is also impossible.

-- Hanna Belov, Lab 4

---

Day 100.

Filed the anomaly report. Standard form. Ref AR-7310. Dr. Chen reviewed it, handed it back, and told me to rerun the tests. I reran them. Same results. She told me to rerun them again.

I understand now that the form isn't for reporting anomalies. The form is for making anomalies disappear.

Suki from Lab 2 transferred out. No notice. Her workstation was cleared by 0600. The samples are still here. Nobody came for them. Nobody came for her things either.

---

Day 104.

Ammunition count: forty-seven rounds, three batteries, one flare. Make them count.

I've stopped filing reports. I've started keeping this instead. The samples from Nemaea Surface are doing something at night that I can't explain with the equipment I've been given. So I requisitioned better equipment. Request denied. Budget code: INSUFFICIENT AUTHORIZATION.

I brought my personal spectrometer. The readings don't match the Mammona-issue unit. Not slightly off. Fundamentally different. Like the standard equipment is calibrated to miss what I'm finding.

That's not a malfunction. That's a decision someone made.

---

Day 113.

Valen Barton approached me after shift. Said they saw my after-hours lab access in the logs. I expected a warning. Instead: "I've been seeing the same thing in the Shimmer. For months. My reports go nowhere too."

We compared data. The correlation is. I don't have a word for it. These aren't coincidences. There's a pattern. The pattern has intent.

I locked the data on a sealed drive. Personal encryption. If the standard equipment is lying to us, I don't trust the standard network either.

---

Day 132.

She gave the order the way orders are given: clearly, once, without looking back.

Dr. Barton didn't show up for shift. Transferred, they said. Same word they used for Suki. Same paperwork. Same empty workstation by morning.

I checked the sealed drive. The data I locked is still there. But there's a new file. I didn't create it. It's a personnel dossier. My personnel dossier. With a field I've never seen before: RETENTION STATUS. The value is PENDING.

---

Day 152.

Something happened last night. I went to check the samples at 0300. They were arranged differently. Not scattered. Arranged. In a pattern I recognized from my own notes. Notes that are on the sealed drive. Notes that nobody has seen.

I don't think I'm studying these samples anymore. I think they're studying me.

-- Hanna Belov

[This datapad was found face-down on the lab bench. The lab was empty. The samples were gone.]

---

The incident log had been updated. The timeline no longer matched her memory. It's not anger. That's what's frightening about it. The colonists in the mess hall are calm. Resolved. They've thought about this. Orion has a list of demands. The list is reasonable. The timing isn't. The bore shaft needs monitoring. The reactor needs hands. Every hour of shutdown is a degree colder.

A handprint appeared on the fogged viewport. From the outside.

**Key NPC:** Orion Kruger (Building: 10, Willpower: 6) -- his building skill determines the approach. He motivation: build something that outlasts the contract. A system, a structure, a legacy.

**Objectives:**
1. Read the demands. They're not unreasonable: medical supplies, rotation schedule, hazard pay, and one thing you can't give them. The truth about what's in the deep bore.
2. Negotiate without violence. The colonists are armed with tools. The security team is armed with worse. The gap between tools and weapons is smaller than anyone thinks.
3. Decide which demands are met, which are promised, and which are refused. The colony's survival depends on getting this right.

**Required Checks:**
- Deception (4+, easy) -- keep your composure under interrogation
- Intimidation (8+, extreme) -- make the informant talk before their nerve breaks
- Negotiation (4+, easy) -- secure passage through contested territory

**If Deception succeeds:** They bought it. Every word. The performance was flawless.
**If Deception fails:** They saw through it. Not the lie itself. The performance. Now they're watching.
**If Intimidation succeeds:** They backed down. The fear is real and useful.
**If Intimidation fails:** Unimpressed. They've seen worse. Now they know you're bluffing.
**If Negotiation succeeds:** Terms accepted. Nobody's happy. That means it's fair.
**If Negotiation fails:** Impasse. The conversation ended politely. Nothing was resolved.

**Conditions:**
- Thermal inversion (instruments unreliable, Research checks at -10)
- Peak shift (full crew present, Stealth checks at disadvantage)
- Reactor at 80% (brownouts in outer sections, Repair checks at -10)

**The Choice:**
Meet every demand. The colony can barely afford it. But the alternative is a workforce that won't work.
OR
Meet the reasonable demands. Refuse the truth about the deep bore. Some things are more dangerous to know than to not know. Tell them that. See if they believe you.

**Twist:**
While the colony's attention is on the mutiny, someone is in the command center. Downloading everything. The mutiny isn't about demands. It's a diversion.

**Faction Stakes:**
- Rust Meridian wants the data encrypted and shipped off-planet. Compliance: colony loses leverage but gains credits
- Iron Shadow Collective wants Orion Kruger extracted. Compliance: you lose a colonist. They gain an asset.
- Nobody in the colony asked for this. Nobody in the colony gets to opt out.

**Consequences (if Choice A):**
- The sealed area is accessible. What's there raises more questions than it answers.
- Orion Kruger gains colony trust. He knows things he didn't before.
- Three colonists file transfer requests. None are approved.

**Consequences (if Choice B):**
- Hab Block Beta stays sealed. The sound from inside doesn't stop.
- Orion Kruger withdraws. Stops talking at meals. He spends shifts alone.
- Iron Shadow Collective makes contact. They know what happened. They have a proposal.

**Outcomes by Roll:**
- Critical success: Clean resolution. No casualties, no complications. The kind of outcome that makes people suspicious.
- Success: Objective complete. One casualty. The casualty was unavoidable. That's what the report will say.
- Failure: The mission fell apart. The pieces are still useful. Rearranged, they form a different picture.
- Critical failure: Objective failed AND new threat introduced. The colony's problems just multiplied.

**Dialogue During Quest:**
- Orion: "Drill output's down twelve percent this week. Same crew. Same equipment. Something's different underground."
- Player: [Respond / Stay Silent / Leave]
- Orion: "I knew about the risks before we shipped out. I came anyway. Figured I deserved the odds."

## QUEST: Last Stand
**Genre:** Escalation | **Tone:** psychic_contamination / cult_devotion
**Location:** Saltcross | **Faction:** Blind Chorus

**Trigger:**
The outer perimeter falls at 2200. The second wall at 2300. By midnight, everything between the colony and what's coming is a single barricade and twenty people who've decided they're not leaving. Orion Kruger is building the barricade out of everything that isn't nailed down. Some things that are.

**Setup:**
A memory of drowning. Vivid. Complete. She'd never been near deep water. The barricade is crude but solid. Mining equipment, supply crates, bed frames. Orion moves through the defenders, checking weapons, checking resolve. Both are running low. Through the barricade gaps, the lights of the colony illuminate the killing ground. Nothing's there yet. Everyone can hear it getting closer.

They spoke in unison. Not rehearsed. Synchronized. Like something else was speaking through them.

**Key NPC:** Orion Kruger (Building: 10, Willpower: 6) -- his building skill determines the approach. He motivation: build something that outlasts the contract. A system, a structure, a legacy.

**Objectives:**
1. Fortify the barricade. You've ninety minutes. Every improvement buys seconds. Seconds matter.
2. Distribute the ammunition. There isn't enough. Every shot has to count. Every shooter has to be placed where they'll do the most good.
3. Hold. When it comes, hold. Don't break. Don't run. There's nowhere to run to.

**Required Checks:**
- Combat (4+, easy) -- defend the reactor during the breach
- Repair (8+, extreme) -- jury-rig the comms array
- Intimidation (8+, extreme) -- stare down the enforcer

**If Combat succeeds:** Controlled violence. The threat is down. The corridor is clear. For now.
**If Combat fails:** The advantage shifted. Someone's bleeding. The situation deteriorated.
**If Repair succeeds:** It holds. The fix is ugly but functional. Good enough for Erebus.
**If Repair fails:** Made it worse. The failure cascaded into two new problems.
**If Intimidation succeeds:** They backed down. The fear is real and useful.
**If Intimidation fails:** Unimpressed. They've seen worse. Now they know you're bluffing.

**Conditions:**
- Blizzard (-15 to Perception checks)
- Peak shift (full crew present, Stealth checks at disadvantage)
- HERMES in maintenance mode (no surveillance for 45 minutes)

**The Choice:**
Send Orion with a team to flank whatever's coming. Aggressive. Risky. Could break the assault before it starts.
OR
Keep everyone behind the wall. Together. Numbers in defense. Let them come to you. Make them pay for every meter.

**Twist:**
Dawn comes. The defenders are alive. The perimeter is wrecked. And in the morning light, Orion sees what they were fighting. Not creatures. Colonists. From the deep bore. Changed. They weren't attacking. They were trying to come home.

**Faction Stakes:**
- Blind Chorus wants to weaponize whatever you find. Compliance: military-grade equipment, but they'll be back for more
- Veil Covenant wants a copy of everything. Compliance: information parity, but now two factions know
- Nobody in the colony asked for this. Nobody in the colony gets to opt out.

**Consequences (if Choice A):**
- the maintenance tunnels reopened. What's inside changes the colony's understanding of the site.
- Orion Kruger gains colony trust. He knows things he didn't before.
- HERMES flags the event in its logs. The flag triggers an automated report to MasTema.

**Consequences (if Choice B):**
- The evidence is destroyed. The questions remain. Nobody asks them out loud.
- Orion Kruger withdraws. Stops talking at meals. He spends shifts alone.
- The next quarterly review goes smoothly. Too smoothly. Someone intervened.

**Outcomes by Roll:**
- Critical success: Clean resolution. No casualties, no complications. The kind of outcome that makes people suspicious.
- Success: Primary objective achieved, secondary compromised. The cost was acceptable. Barely.
- Failure: The mission fell apart. The pieces are still useful. Rearranged, they form a different picture.
- Critical failure: Total loss. The situation is worse than before the attempt. And now they know you tried.

**Dialogue During Quest:**
- Orion: "Don't leave me here. Not in the dark."
- Player: [Respond / Stay Silent / Leave]
- Orion: "I knew about the risks before we shipped out. I came anyway. Figured I deserved the odds."

**Reward:** 6 thermal cores, a key to a room that isn't on any map

### [SEQ:91] [Quest] [22:52:52]
============================================================

## QUEST: Descent
**Genre:** Expedition | **Tone:** dissociation / paranoid
**Location:** Buried City of Khem | **Faction:** Order of the Bone Parish

**Trigger:**
The drill team punches through the floor of the deepest shaft. Below it: a void. Not a cave. A void. The instruments say it goes down another six hundred meters. Isa Venin says the drill mapping only goes to two hundred. The rest is unmapped.

**Setup:**
The descent pod creaks on its cable. Below, the bore shaft narrows, then opens into something vast. Sounds came from very far away. Her own voice was the farthest. Isa runs the spotlight across the void. The walls aren't rock. They're smooth. Worked. Someone carved this space. Or something grew it. The air coming from below is warm. Warmer than it should be. And it moves. Like breathing.

She counted the footsteps behind her. They matched hers. Exactly.

**Key NPC:** Isa Venin (Mining: 9, Willpower: 6) -- their mining skill determines the approach. They motivation: get off Erebus by any means. Legal, illegal, doesn't matter.

**Objectives:**
1. Descend to the void floor. Map the space. The cable reaches. Barely.
2. Collect samples from the worked walls. The material doesn't match any known geology. It's not stone. It's not metal. It resists the drill and yields to the hand.
3. Find the heat source. The temperature increases as you descend. At the bottom, it's twenty degrees above freezing. Something is generating heat. A lot of it.

**Required Checks:**
- Combat (5+, normal) -- defend the reactor during the breach
- Survival (8+, extreme) -- ration the remaining supplies for the team
- Mining (6+, hard) -- extract the thermal cores from unstable rock

**If Combat succeeds:** Controlled violence. The threat is down. The corridor is clear. For now.
**If Combat fails:** The advantage shifted. Someone's bleeding. The situation deteriorated.
**If Survival succeeds:** Found the path. Found the shelter. Found the will to keep moving.
**If Survival fails:** The cold got in. The shortcut wasn't. Lost time and supplies.
**If Mining succeeds:** The passage opens. Behind it: a room that shouldn't exist. Pre-colony construction.
**If Mining fails:** The collapse spreads. The passage is gone. But the sound from the other side continues.

**Conditions:**
- Thermal inversion (instruments unreliable, Research checks at -10)
- Supply window (limited time before the shuttle departs)
- Lockdown protocol active (all bulkheads sealed, movement restricted)

**The Choice:**
Go deeper. The unmapped section calls. The air is warm. The walls are strange. Whatever is down there, it's big enough to heat the air for six hundred meters.
OR
Stop. Map what you've found. Report it. Come back with more equipment. More people. The smart play. The one that lets whatever's down there prepare for your return.

**Twist:**
The void isn't empty. At the bottom, arranged in concentric circles, are pods. Thousands of them. Sealed. Warm. Something is inside each one. Some of them are moving.

**Faction Stakes:**
- Order of the Bone Parish wants the situation contained. No reports. No questions. Compliance: nothing happens to you. That's the reward.
- United Terran Colonies wants to negotiate directly. Compliance: bypasses colony authority. Sets a precedent.
- Nobody in the colony asked for this. Nobody in the colony gets to opt out.

**Consequences (if Choice A):**
- Section B reopened. What's inside changes the colony's understanding of the site.
- Isa Venin's arc shifts from 'suspicious' to 'vindicated.'
- HERMES flags the event in its logs. The flag triggers an automated report to MasTema.

**Consequences (if Choice B):**
- The situation is contained. On paper. The nightmares aren't on paper.
- Isa Venin's arc shifts from 'suspicious' to 'paranoid.'
- The next quarterly review goes smoothly. Too smoothly. Someone intervened.

**Outcomes by Roll:**
- Critical success: Both objectives achieved without cost. The colony gains leverage and resources.
- Success: Primary objective achieved, secondary compromised. The cost was acceptable. Barely.
- Failure: The mission fell apart. The pieces are still useful. Rearranged, they form a different picture.
- Critical failure: Total loss. The situation is worse than before the attempt. And now they know you tried.

**Dialogue During Quest:**
- Isa: "Don't walk the corridors alone past 0200. That's not policy. That's experience."
- Player: [Respond / Stay Silent / Leave]
- Isa: "I did something. On my last posting. I can't undo it."

**Reward:** 5 thermal cores, the previous site manager's journal

### [SEQ:94] [Data Pad] [22:52:53]
============================================================

## DATA PAD: Personal Journal -- Margaux Steelberg
**Found at:** Pale Harbor | **Tone:** corporate_dystopia | **Type:** journal

---

Day 3. Or 4. The clock in the mess is wrong again and nobody fixes it because nobody cares anymore.

The memo was seven pages long. The word 'death' didn't appear. The word 'attrition' appeared nine times.

First impressions: it's exactly what the brochure promised if you read between the lines. Cold. Grey. The kind of place where the word 'amenities' means 'there's a roof.' The ShockPop machine in the corridor works, which is more than I expected. Met my bunkmate. Esperanza Larsen. She works the drill. Doesn't talk much. Fine by me.

Keeping this journal because I promised. A record. Proof I was here. Proof I was me.

---

Day 9.

Getting the rhythm. Shift starts at 0600. NutriLoaf for breakfast. The work is work. I'm a corpse handler here, same as I was on the last posting. The cold's different though. It gets into the walls, the food, the conversations. Not just temperature. Atmosphere.

Esperanza said something strange at dinner: "Count the people in the mess every morning. If the number changes, don't ask why." I laughed. She didn't.

---

Day 24.

The quarterly report described eleven deaths as 'personnel throughput adjustment.'

Okay. So. I'm going to write this down because writing it down makes it real and if it's real then I'm not imagining it and if I'm not imagining it then I need to deal with it.

The wall in the maintenance tunnel is warm. Not heated-by-pipes warm. Warm like skin. And it pulses. I put my hand on it. I shouldn't have put my hand on it.

I asked Esperanza about it. She said: "Yeah." Just that. Yeah. Like I'd finally noticed the weather.

---

Day 38.

Can't sleep. Thought it was the cold but it's not the cold. It's the quiet. Not silence. There's always noise here, generators, pipes, wind. It's that the quiet is underneath the noise. Like the noise is a blanket over something that's listening.

The holiday bonus was a Sunny Fizz voucher. Redeemable at participating locations. There were no participating locations.

Esperanza hasn't been to her bunk in three nights. She shows up for shift. Eats. Works. But at lights out, she goes somewhere else. I followed her last night. Stopped at Section D. The door was open. It shouldn't be open. I didn't go in.

I'm not going to go in.

My hands are shaking as I write this. That's new.

---

Day 71.

Found a note under my mattress. My handwriting. I didn't write it. It says: 'STOP LOOKING.' I don't know what I was looking at.

I want to go home. I keep saying that word, home, and each time it means less. Like a word you repeat until it's just sounds.

---

Day 83.

I went into Section D last night.

Esperanza was there.

Everyone was there.

[The remaining pages contain a single symbol, repeated. It matches no known writing system. Analysis pending. Analysis has been pending for 6 months.]

---

**Objectives:**
1. Run a full biometric comparison. Fingerprints, retinal scan, DNA. The results are 96% match. Not 100%. Not close enough.
2. Access the original personnel file from Cassian's hiring records at Palehold. The records show a different person with the same name. Different face. Same employment history. Same memories.
3. Confront Cassian with the discrepancy. Watch their face. The confusion is genuine. The fear is real. They don't know who they're either.

**Required Checks:**
- Social (6+, hard) -- convince them you're on their side
- Deception (5+, normal) -- pass as authorized personnel
- Perception (8+, extreme) -- spot the tripwire before it's too late

**If Social succeeds:** Trust earned. The hard way. The only way that lasts.
**If Social fails:** The walls went up. Whatever trust existed just evaporated.
**If Deception succeeds:** They bought it. Every word. The performance was flawless.
**If Deception fails:** They saw through it. Not the lie itself. The performance. Now they're watching.
**If Perception succeeds:** There it is. The detail everyone missed. It changes the equation.
**If Perception fails:** Looked right at it. Didn't see it. The brain filtered it out as normal.

**Conditions:**
- Blizzard (-15 to Perception checks)
- Supply window (limited time before the shuttle departs)
- Lockdown protocol active (all bulkheads sealed, movement restricted)

**The Choice:**
Help Cassian investigate their own past. Follow the trail back to Palehold. Find the original. If there's one.
OR
Suggest Cassian stop looking. Some questions don't have answers. Some answers aren't survivable.

**Twist:**
The file is correct. Cassian is the imposter. But not deliberately. Someone rewrote their memories. Gave them a life. A name. A reason to be here. The real question isn't who Cassian is. It's who sent them.

**Faction Stakes:**
- Order of the Bone Parish wants the data encrypted and shipped off-planet. Compliance: colony loses leverage but gains credits
- Cult of the Abyss wants a copy of everything. Compliance: information parity, but now two factions know
- The colonists don't know about this yet. When they find out, morale takes the hit regardless of outcome.

**Consequences (if Choice A):**
- The sealed area is accessible. What's there raises more questions than it answers.
- Cassian Bakshi is compromised. Order of the Bone Parish has something on him now.
- Order of the Bone Parish sends a follow-up team. The team asks questions nobody wants answered.

**Consequences (if Choice B):**
- The situation is contained. On paper. The nightmares aren't on paper.
- Cassian Bakshi requests reassignment. The request sits in a queue that doesn't move.
- Two weeks later, a supply crate arrives with no manifest. Inside: a Rock Crablet shell polished into a pendant.

**Outcomes by Roll:**
- Critical success: Clean resolution. No casualties, no complications. The kind of outcome that makes people suspicious.
- Success: Primary objective achieved, secondary compromised. The cost was acceptable. Barely.
- Failure: The mission fell apart. The pieces are still useful. Rearranged, they form a different picture.
- Critical failure: Objective failed AND new threat introduced. The colony's problems just multiplied.

**Dialogue During Quest:**
- Cassian: "Don't tell anyone I asked you. Promise me. Don't tell anyone."
- Player: [Respond / Stay Silent / Leave]
- Cassian: "The night shift has rules. Follow them. Even the ones that sound crazy."

**Reward:** 6 thermal cores, new NPC ally

### [SEQ:98] [Quest] [22:52:53]
============================================================

## QUEST: Reactor Critical
**Genre:** Escalation | **Tone:** cult_devotion / isolation
**Location:** Hyades | **Faction:** Void Serpents

**Trigger:**
The reactor alarm screams at 0400. Not the overheat warning. Not the maintenance alert. The alarm nobody has ever heard before because it's never been triggered. The one labeled 'CASCADE FAILURE.' Kira Nakamura runs to the control room. The core temperature is climbing. Fast.

**Setup:**
The reactor is a Frostpunk-style thermal generator. It heats the colony. It powers the lights, the water, the air recyclers. Without it, the colony dies. Slowly. In the cold. The leader said it was true. That was the end of the discussion. Kira reads the gauges. Core temperature: 340%. Rising. Containment integrity: declining. 'We've maybe six hours,' Kira says. 'Then it either melts down or blows. Neither is good.'

The sound of their own breathing had become company. They talked back to it.

**Key NPC:** Kira Nakamura (Research: 10, Willpower: 3) -- her research skill determines the approach. She motivation: become indispensable. The person nobody can afford to lose.

**Objectives:**
1. Diagnose the failure. The cascade started in the coolant system. The coolant is gone. Not leaked. Drained. Deliberately.
2. Find replacement coolant. The backup tanks are in the lower levels. Past the bore shaft entrance. The temperature down there's already climbing.
3. Fix the reactor or prepare for evacuation. Six hours. The clock is real.

**Required Checks:**
- Survival (8+, extreme) -- cross the unstable terrain without incident
- Repair (5+, normal) -- fix the filtration system before the air goes bad
- Intimidation (5+, normal) -- force the crew to comply without violence

**If Survival succeeds:** Found the path. Found the shelter. Found the will to keep moving.
**If Survival fails:** The cold got in. The shortcut wasn't. Lost time and supplies.
**If Repair succeeds:** It holds. The fix is ugly but functional. Good enough for Erebus.
**If Repair fails:** Made it worse. The failure cascaded into two new problems.
**If Intimidation succeeds:** They backed down. The fear is real and useful.
**If Intimidation fails:** Unimpressed. They've seen worse. Now they know you're bluffing.

**Conditions:**
- Wind chill advisory (-10 to all outdoor checks)
- Peak shift (full crew present, Stealth checks at disadvantage)
- Reactor at 80% (brownouts in outer sections, Repair checks at -10)

**The Choice:**
Fix the reactor. Send a team into the irradiated zone to replace the coolant lines. Dangerous work. Essential work. The team will take doses. How much depends on how fast they work.
OR
Scram the reactor. Emergency shutdown. The colony goes dark. In these temperatures, dark means cold. Cold means dead. But at least not exploded.

**Twist:**
The coolant wasn't drained by sabotage. The reactor consumed it. The thermal core at the reactor's heart isn't a power source. It's an egg. And the rising temperature is an incubation cycle. Something is about to hatch.

**Faction Stakes:**
- Void Serpents wants the evidence destroyed. Compliance: +reputation, -23 thermal cores as 'bonus'
- Vanguard Alliance wants the site destroyed. Compliance: the evidence is gone. So is whatever else was down there.
- Nobody in the colony asked for this. Nobody in the colony gets to opt out.

**Consequences (if Choice A):**
- The evidence is preserved. It's leverage now. The question is who holds it.
- Kira Nakamura's arc shifts from 'suspicious' to 'vindicated.'
- Morale drops for a week. Then stabilizes. The new normal is lower than the old one.

**Consequences (if Choice B):**
- The situation is contained. On paper. The nightmares aren't on paper.
- Kira Nakamura withdraws. Stops talking at meals. She spends shifts alone.
- Two weeks later, a supply crate arrives with no manifest. Inside: a ZapNoodles Xtreme cup used as a planter for something growing.

**Outcomes by Roll:**
- Critical success: Clean resolution. No casualties, no complications. The kind of outcome that makes people suspicious.
- Success: Done. Not clean, not elegant, but done. The colony moves forward.
- Failure: The mission fell apart. The pieces are still useful. Rearranged, they form a different picture.
- Critical failure: Catastrophic. Not just failure. Escalation. What was a problem is now a crisis.

**Dialogue During Quest:**
- Kira: "You're the only one I can ask."
- Player: [Respond / Stay Silent / Leave]
- Kira: "Don't open sealed doors without checking the pressure gauge first. Lost a guy that way."

**Reward:** 12 thermal cores, medical supplies (enough for two emergencies)

## HISTORY: The Listening Post
**Era:** corporate | **Tone:** the_uncanny

The new transfer smiled. Too wide. The muscles in their face didn't quite coordinate.

Mammona's records show 6 supply drops to this site over 7 years. The colony's own records show 12. The difference is 2 drops. Nobody can account for what they delivered.

**Significance:** Mammona's records don't match reality. That's either incompetence or intent. Mammona isn't incompetent.

**Mechanical Impact:**
- Colony morale: -3 for three days (the news spreads)
- the lower levels: sealed (inaccessible until quest completes)
- NPC Kira Nakamura: arc shifts to 'paranoid'
- Thermal core output in the affected area drops 10%. Cause: undetermined.

**Evidence:**
- Maintenance log #4122 (references a 'routine personnel transfer' on the same date)
- A bloodstain on the ceiling of the maintenance crawlspace. The ceiling is three meters up.
- A photograph found in Hanna Marr's quarters. Shows a room that doesn't exist in the colony
- HERMES logged a 'scheduled maintenance window' during the event. No maintenance was scheduled.

**Who Knows:**
- **Rolf Schmidt:** filed a report afterward. The report was rejected. They filed it again. Rejected again.
- **Kira Nakamura:** has been asking questions. The questions are making people uncomfortable.
- **Nikolai Deepwell:** has no connection to the event. But they've been dreaming about it. Accurately.

**Aftermath:**
- A new restricted area was designated. The restriction applies to everyone. Including the person who designated it.
- Two faction operatives were seen near Precursor Ruins (North Ridge) the following week. They didn't enter. They measured something.
- Someone started leaving offerings near the site. Small things. Food, water, a folded note. Nobody claims responsibility.

**HERMES Analysis:**
HERMES's response to queries about this event changed on Day 65. Before: detailed, factual, cooperative. After: 'Please direct inquiries to your site manager.' The site manager was not informed of this change.

**Related Incidents:**
A similar event was recorded at Karnaith Lower Decks in 2543. The similarities were noted by one analyst. The analyst was reassigned.

**Investigation Check:**
- Social (6+, hard) -- dig deeper into what happened
- **If successful:** the evidence leads to a sealed drive in the maintenance crawlspace. The drive is still warm.
- **If failed:** the trail goes cold. Cleaned. Every surface, every log, every witness memory. Sanitized in the last 48 hours by someone thorough.

### [SEQ:111] [Quest] [22:52:54]
============================================================

## QUEST: Quarantine
**Genre:** Survival Horror | **Tone:** exhaustion / isolation
**Location:** Port Meridian | **Faction:** Bitter Circuit

**Trigger:**
Thea Rathmore collapses during shift. The medic runs a contamination panel. The results come back in a color the medic hasn't seen before. Thea is isolated within minutes. Within hours, two more colonists show symptoms.

**Setup:**
The quarantine bay was built for four. There are seven inside now. The shift ended. Moving required a decision she wasn't ready to make. Through the observation window, Thea watches the player with eyes that are too calm. 'I can feel it working,' Thea says. 'That's the worst part. I can feel it and it doesn't hurt.'

The perimeter was quiet. That used to be a relief.

**Key NPC:** Thea Rathmore (Mining: 8, Willpower: 4) -- her mining skill determines the approach. She motivation: discover something valuable enough to buy freedom. Thermal cores, precursor tech, Mammona secrets.

**Objectives:**
1. Determine the infection vector. It's not airborne. It's not contact. It's not water. It's something else.
2. Keep the quarantine sealed while Bitter Circuit demands access to study the infected. Their 'study' involves a scalpel and a shipping container.
3. Find a treatment before the infected reach stage three. Nobody's seen stage three yet. The medical database has a file on it. The file is just the word 'irreversible.'

**Required Checks:**
- Medical (5+, normal) -- determine if the tissue sample is human
- Stealth (6+, hard) -- move through the restricted section undetected
- Perception (6+, hard) -- read the room during the negotiation

**If Medical succeeds:** The diagnosis is clear. Treatment is possible. Barely. But possible.
**If Medical fails:** Missed the critical symptom. The window for treatment is closing.
**If Stealth succeeds:** In and out. They'll never know anyone was there. The data is secure.
**If Stealth fails:** A sound. A shadow. Someone turned their head. The window is gone.
**If Perception succeeds:** There it is. The detail everyone missed. It changes the equation.
**If Perception fails:** Looked right at it. Didn't see it. The brain filtered it out as normal.

**Conditions:**
- Thermal inversion (instruments unreliable, Research checks at -10)
- 0300 hours (fatigue penalties, -5 to Perception)
- HERMES in maintenance mode (no surveillance for 45 minutes)

**The Choice:**
Expand the quarantine to the entire hab block. Forty percent of the colony locked down. Possibly for nothing.
OR
Keep the quarantine small and tight. If it's already spread beyond the bay, this is a death sentence for everyone who's already exposed.

**Twist:**
Thea was patient zero, but not from this outbreak. This is the second time. The first was on Port Meridian. Thea survived. The colony didn't.

**Faction Stakes:**
- Bitter Circuit wants to weaponize whatever you find. Compliance: military-grade equipment, but they'll be back for more
- StarByte Vends wants the site destroyed. Compliance: the evidence is gone. So is whatever else was down there.
- The colony just wants to survive the week. Both options cost them something.

**Consequences (if Choice A):**
- The sealed area is accessible. What's there raises more questions than it answers.
- Thea Rathmore's arc shifts from 'suspicious' to 'vindicated.'
- Bitter Circuit sends a follow-up team. The team asks questions nobody wants answered.

**Consequences (if Choice B):**
- The situation is contained. On paper. The nightmares aren't on paper.
- Thea Rathmore's arc shifts from 'suspicious' to 'paranoid.'
- The next quarterly review goes smoothly. Too smoothly. Someone intervened.

**Outcomes by Roll:**
- Critical success: Both objectives achieved without cost. The colony gains leverage and resources.
- Success: Objective complete. One casualty. The casualty was unavoidable. That's what the report will say.
- Failure: Objective failed, but information gained. The failure teaches more than success would have.
- Critical failure: Catastrophic. Not just failure. Escalation. What was a problem is now a crisis.

**Dialogue During Quest:**
- Thea: "The shift handover notes are getting shorter. Used to be a full page. Now it's a sentence. 'Same as yesterday.'"
- Player: [Respond / Stay Silent / Leave]
- Thea: "Stay inside the perimeter. I'm not asking."

**Reward:** 9 thermal cores, schematics for equipment Mammona doesn't ship to postings

### [SEQ:120] [Data Pad] [22:52:55]
============================================================

## DATA PAD: Personal Journal -- Hasan Dranth
**Found at:** Eclipse's End | **Tone:** hypervigilance | **Type:** journal

---

Day 3. Or 4. The clock in the mess is wrong again and nobody fixes it because nobody cares anymore.

The door opened and three things happened at once: hand to weapon, body sideways, eyes on the entryway.

First impressions: it's exactly what the brochure promised if you read between the lines. Cold. Grey. The kind of place where the word 'amenities' means 'there's a roof.' The NutriLoaf machine in the corridor works, which is more than I expected. Met my bunkmate. Tomas Okonkwo. He works the drill. Doesn't talk much. Fine by me.

Keeping this journal because I promised. A record. Proof I was here. Proof I was me.

---

Day 9.

Getting the rhythm. Shift starts at 0600. NutriLoaf for breakfast. The work is work. I'm a anomaly surveyor here, same as I was on the last posting. The cold's different though. It gets into the walls, the food, the conversations. Not just temperature. Atmosphere.

Tomas said something strange at dinner: "Don't go past Section A after lights out. Nobody tells you that. I'm telling you." I laughed. He didn't.

---

Day 26.

She tracked every sound. The vent cycle. The generator rhythm. Footsteps at eighty meters.

Okay. So. I'm going to write this down because writing it down makes it real and if it's real then I'm not imagining it and if I'm not imagining it then I need to deal with it.

The shadows in the corridor outside Hab 14 don't match the light sources. I checked. Three times.

I asked Tomas about it. He said: "Yeah." Just that. Yeah. Like I'd finally noticed the weather.

---

Day 46.

Can't sleep. Thought it was the cold but it's not the cold. It's the quiet. Not silence. There's always noise here, generators, pipes, wind. It's that the quiet is underneath the noise. Like the noise is a blanket over something that's listening.

Sleep happened in forty-minute intervals. Any longer felt like dying.

Tomas hasn't been to his bunk in three nights. He shows up for shift. Eats. Works. But at lights out, he goes somewhere else. I followed him last night. Stopped at Section A. The door was open. It shouldn't be open. I didn't go in.

I'm not going to go in.

My hands are shaking as I write this. That's new.

---

Day 64.

Mammona sent a psych evaluation form. I filled it out honestly. The results came back 'within normal parameters.' Every question. I said I was hearing things. Normal parameters. I said I was seeing things. Normal parameters. I said I was afraid. Normal. Parameters.

I want to go home. I keep saying that word, home, and each time it means less. Like a word you repeat until it's just sounds.

---

Today I looked in the mirror and for the first time in weeks, my reflection was doing the same thing I was doing. I should've been relieved. Instead I thought: what was it doing all those other times?

[This datapad was found in the recycling queue. The owner's bunk was empty. Personal effects: undisturbed. Contract status: active.]

---

**Cross-reference:** See historical record 'The Surplus Drops'

### [SEQ:125] [Quest] [22:52:56]
============================================================

## QUEST: Divided Colony
**Genre:** Faction Tension | **Tone:** agoraphobia / tender
**Location:** Ashbreak | **Faction:** StarByte Vends

**Trigger:**
The thermal core vein in the cargo bay is the richest strike the colony has seen. StarByte Vends wants it mined for corporate quota. Rolf Schmidt wants it rationed for colony survival. Both have backing. The colony splits down the middle.

**Setup:**
Two factions. Two agendas. One resource. The blizzard stopped and the landscape was a white blank. Nowhere to hide. Rolf holds a colony meeting in the mess hall. Half the colonists sit on Rolf's side. Half sit across. The line down the middle of the room is invisible and absolute.

He hummed while he worked. The same song, every shift. It made the silence bearable.

**Key NPC:** Rolf Schmidt (Hunting: 9, Willpower: 6) -- his hunting skill determines the approach. He motivation: master the bore shafts. Know them better than anyone alive. Own the knowledge that keeps the colony running.

**Objectives:**
1. Mediate between Rolf and StarByte Vends's representative. Find a compromise. If one exists.
2. Determine the actual yield of the thermal core vein. Both sides are inflating their numbers. The truth is somewhere in between. And worse than either estimate.
3. Prevent the tension from escalating to violence. Two colonists have already been in a fight. The next one will involve tools.

**Required Checks:**
- Intimidation (5+, normal) -- stare down the enforcer
- Negotiation (8+, extreme) -- talk the hostage-taker into releasing the medic
- Social (8+, extreme) -- read the crew's mood before making the call

**If Intimidation succeeds:** They backed down. The fear is real and useful.
**If Intimidation fails:** Unimpressed. They've seen worse. Now they know you're bluffing.
**If Negotiation succeeds:** Terms accepted. Nobody's happy. That means it's fair.
**If Negotiation fails:** Impasse. The conversation ended politely. Nothing was resolved.
**If Social succeeds:** Trust earned. The hard way. The only way that lasts.
**If Social fails:** The walls went up. Whatever trust existed just evaporated.

**Conditions:**
- Whiteout conditions (-20 to navigation, +10 to Stealth)
- Night shift (reduced visibility, +10 to Stealth)
- HERMES in maintenance mode (no surveillance for 45 minutes)

**The Choice:**
Split the vein. Half for quota, half for colony. Neither side gets enough. Both resent the compromise. But nobody dies today.
OR
Seize the vein yourself. Colony authority. Neither faction controls it. Both become your enemy. But you control the resource.

**Twist:**
The vein isn't thermal cores. Not entirely. Something else is mixed in. Something alive. Mining it's waking it up.

**Faction Stakes:**
- StarByte Vends wants the evidence destroyed. Compliance: +reputation, -10 thermal cores as 'bonus'
- BioVault Inc. wants to negotiate directly. Compliance: bypasses colony authority. Sets a precedent.
- Nobody in the colony asked for this. Nobody in the colony gets to opt out.

**Consequences (if Choice A):**
- the cargo bay reopened. What's inside changes the colony's understanding of the site.
- Rolf Schmidt gains colony trust. He knows things he didn't before.
- Morale drops for a week. Then stabilizes. The new normal is lower than the old one.

**Consequences (if Choice B):**
- The situation is contained. On paper. The nightmares aren't on paper.
- Rolf Schmidt requests reassignment. The request sits in a queue that doesn't move.
- Nikolai Deepwell starts asking questions. The questions are pointed.

**Outcomes by Roll:**
- Critical success: Both objectives achieved without cost. The colony gains leverage and resources.
- Success: Objective complete. One casualty. The casualty was unavoidable. That's what the report will say.
- Failure: Objective failed, but information gained. The failure teaches more than success would have.
- Critical failure: Objective failed AND new threat introduced. The colony's problems just multiplied.

**Dialogue During Quest:**
- Rolf: "NutriLoaf batch forty-seven tastes different. Not worse. Different. Like pennies. Nobody can name how."
- Player: [Respond / Stay Silent / Leave]
- Rolf: "I've been sending reports to someone outside the colony. I can't say who. I'm not even sure anymore."

**Reward:** 3 thermal cores, schematics for equipment Mammona doesn't ship to postings

- **If successful:** Clean shot. The weapon performs exactly as designed. The target doesn't.
- **If failed:** The discharge is wrong. Too loud, too bright, too slow. Something in the mechanism hesitated.

**Maintenance Requirements:**
- Interval: after each use in sub-zero conditions
- If neglected: the weapon develops a delay between trigger pull and discharge

**Malfunction Chance:** 3% per engagement
- the weapon fires but the round doesn't leave the barrel. The next trigger pull will be interesting.

The kill marks on this weapon match unsolved incidents across two postings. The incidents were classified as 'accidental.' The pattern suggests otherwise.

### [SEQ:127] [Data Pad] [22:52:56]
============================================================

## DATA PAD: Research Log -- Zuri Chen
**Found at:** Oasis Outpost Three | **Tone:** gaslighting | **Type:** research log

---

Day 116.

They said she'd approved the transfer. Her signature was on the form. She'd never seen the form.

I wasn't looking for anomalies. I was running standard assays on material recovered from Oasis Outpost Three. That's what makes this worse. A standard assay. Routine. And then the mass spectrometer returned a molecular weight that doesn't correspond to any element on the periodic table.

Not a compound. Not an alloy. An element. One that shouldn't exist. neural control chips has been sitting in this lab for two weeks and nobody noticed because nobody ran the right test. I ran the right test. I wish I hadn't.

-- Zuri Chen, Lab 4

---

Day 118.

Filed the anomaly report. Standard form. Ref AR-9430. Dr. Orosco reviewed it, handed it back, and told me to rerun the tests. I reran them. Same results. She told me to rerun them again.

I understand now that the form isn't for reporting anomalies. The form is for making anomalies disappear.

Fritz from Lab 2 transferred out. No notice. His workstation was cleared by 0600. The samples are still here. Nobody came for them. Nobody came for his things either.

---

Day 124.

HERMES confirmed the temperature was stable. Her breath fogged. HERMES confirmed the temperature was stable.

I've stopped filing reports. I've started keeping this instead. The samples from Oasis Outpost Three are doing something at night that I can't explain with the equipment I've been given. So I requisitioned better equipment. Request denied. Budget code: INSUFFICIENT AUTHORIZATION.

I brought my personal spectrometer. The readings don't match the Mammona-issue unit. Not slightly off. Fundamentally different. Like the standard equipment is calibrated to miss what I'm finding.

That's not a malfunction. That's a decision someone made.

---

Day 141.

Quinn Blackwell approached me after shift. Said they saw my after-hours lab access in the logs. I expected a warning. Instead: "I've been seeing the same thing in the Xenolith. For months. My reports go nowhere too."

We compared data. The correlation is. I don't have a word for it. These aren't coincidences. There's a pattern. The pattern has intent.

I locked the data on a sealed drive. Personal encryption. If the standard equipment is lying to us, I don't trust the standard network either.

---

Day 144.

The report said clear. She'd measured the contamination herself. The report said clear.

Dr. Blackwell didn't show up for shift. Transferred, they said. Same word they used for Fritz. Same paperwork. Same empty workstation by morning.

I checked the sealed drive. The data I locked is still there. But there's a new file. I didn't create it. It's a personnel dossier. My personnel dossier. With a field I've never seen before: RETENTION STATUS. The value is PENDING.

---

Day 167.

Check cabinet 8. The real readings are taped to the back panel. Compare them to what's in the system. Then decide what kind of person you want to be.

-- Zuri Chen

[No further entries. The lab was reassigned on Day 174.]

---

**Cross-reference:** See historical record 'The Listening Post'

- Data: wall-mounted displays cycling through data that changes when read. (Research check, difficulty: hard)

- Day 88: Three separate colonists reported the same dream involving the site. None had been there.

- If mined: extraction reveals a hollow space behind the vein. The space is occupied.
- If sealed: HERMES objects. Silently. By rerouting maintenance schedules to avoid the area.

**Found Here:**
- dog tags for three people. Two names match colony records. The third matches nobody.
- three identical photographs of the same hallway taken decades apart. Nothing has changed. Nothing.
- A data pad: "Three words, written in something that isn't ink: STOP DIGGING DOWN."

**Location Secrets:**
- A room exists on the lower level that isn't on any schematic. The room has power. The room has been cleaned recently.
- The site has been photographed by satellite every 72 hours since the colony was established. In 40% of images, the site casts a shadow that doesn't match the sun's position.
- One wall isn't a wall. It's a membrane. It responds to pressure. It responds to sound. It might respond to intent.

**What Happened Here:**
Something happened here during the corporate era. The records were purged. Not redacted. Purged. The difference is: redacted records leave a shape. These left nothing.
**Connected NPC:** Rowan Yamamoto -- was assigned here on a previous posting. The posting isn't in their file.

**Active Events:**
- [mechanical] three consoles in the operations room displayed the same error simultaneously. The error code isn't in the manual. (duration: 219 ticks)
- [environmental] ice forming on interior surfaces despite heating. The crystals follow the wiring pattern. (duration: 323 ticks)
- [social] the mess hall's seating arrangement changed overnight. Nobody moved their seat consciously. (duration: 137 ticks)

### [SEQ:136] [Data Pad] [22:52:57]

## DATA PAD: Maintenance Log -- Corinna Bakshi
**Found at:** Subsurface Melt Lake | **Tone:** dread | **Type:** maintenance log

---

**MAINTENANCE LOG -- Water Recycler Unit 3**
**Tech:** Corinna Bakshi (CB-687)
**Date:** Day 63

Routine inspection. All parameters within spec. Filter replacement completed. Calibration nominal. Estimated next service: Day 93.

Notes: None. Clean run.

-- CB-687

---

**Date:** Day 75

Unscheduled check. Night shift reported condensation forming on the exterior despite sub-zero ambient. Inspected. Couldn't reproduce. All readings nominal at time of inspection.

Action: monitoring. Will revisit next scheduled maintenance.

-- CB-687

---

**Date:** Day 83

Something clicked in the wall. Not mechanical. Biological.

Follow-up on previous entry. The deviation has recurred. Same magnitude. Same duration. Same time: 0300.

Submitted work order for diagnostic overhaul. Status: queued. Estimated wait: 6 weeks.

Something isn't right. I don't have data to support that statement. After 25 years of fixing machines, you develop a feeling in your hands. The feeling says something isn't right.

-- CB-687

---

**Date:** Day 100

Diagnostic overhaul completed. 8 hours of testing. Every component individually verified. Every sensor calibrated. Every connection checked.

Result: the system is operating perfectly. Better than perfectly. Efficiency is up 5% from installation baseline. That shouldn't be possible on equipment this age with this service history.

But the sound is still there. And now I can hear it from the corridor. And now it has a rhythm. And the rhythm matches the drill cycle at Deep Bore Alpha. Water Recycler Unit 3 has no connection to the drill. No shared power bus, no shared conduit, no shared anything. There's no mechanical path for that vibration to travel. But it's here.

I'm filing this under 'resolved, nominal' because that's what the data says. The data is wrong. I don't know how to file that.

-- CB-687

---

**Date:** Day 106

The air pressure changed. Just enough to make her ears pop. The gauge read normal.

I found something behind the access panel that shouldn't be there. Not a component. A cavity. Small. The size of a fist. The interior surface is smooth in a way that machined metal isn't smooth. In a way that nothing manufactured is smooth. And there's something in it. Small. Warm. I didn't touch it.

I closed the panel. I'm not going to open it again.

I'm not going to file this.

-- CB-687

[No further entries in this log. Subsequent maintenance logs for Water Recycler Unit 3 are filed by a different technician. They describe the system as 'nominal.']

---

Dalia,

Dalia,

-- Lily

[Written in two colors of ink. The color changes correspond to no obvious pattern.]

Dalia,

I've been writing these like reports because reports are safe. Reports have structure. What's happening doesn't have structure.

I need you to remember everything I've written. If something happens, the details matter.

---

**FOLLOW-UP:** Day 72
**CLASSIFICATION:** Restricted

**CLASSIFICATION:** Restricted / Protocol 7

HERMES's logs for the relevant timeframe show a 18-second gap. Gaps in HERMES logs should not be possible.

I have requested consultation with a specialist. Request forwarded to MasTema. No response.

-- Dr. Elena Venin

---

**CLASSIFICATION:** Personal / Not Filed

I'm no longer confident this is a medical issue. I'm no longer confident in the word 'issue.' Patient is calm. Genuinely calm. Not medicated calm. Not dissociated calm. Unless the improvement is the disease. Unless what I'm calling improvement is something else wearing a familiar shape.

I don't know anymore. I'm filing this report because filing reports is what I do. I don't know what else to do.

-- Dr. Elena Venin

Doctor Venin's notes are thorough and accurate. The observations are described. What they mean is not.

Recommend immediate

## HISTORY: Recycler Contamination
**Era:** present | **Tone:** sudden_dread

She sneezed and tasted blood. When she wiped her nose, the blood was black.

Three survey teams preceded yours. Team 1's report was filed on Day 56. Team 2's report contradicted it. Team 3's report was never filed.

**Significance:** The previous crew encountered something they couldn't explain. They explained it anyway, and the explanation is worse than the mystery.

**Mechanical Impact:**
- Colony morale: -12 for until resolved (the news spreads)
- Section B: sealed (inaccessible until quest completes)
- NPC Kira Nakamura: arc shifts to 'vindicated'
- HERMES begins logging increased activity in the area. The logs are not shared.

**Evidence:**
- Maintenance log #7676 (references nothing. The entry for that date is blank. Every other entry is filled.)
- Scorch marks on the corridor wall of Section E (painted over, visible under UV)
- A data drive hidden in the wall panel of Bunk 3. Encrypted. Personal key.
- HERMES flagged the event internally, then removed the flag. The removal is logged. The original flag is not.

**Who Knows:**
- **Caspian Han:** filed a report afterward. The report was rejected. They filed it again. Rejected again.
- **Luca Bakshi:** heard about it secondhand. Has theories. The theories are wrong but close.
- **Orion Kruger:** knows nothing. Arrived after. But found something in their quarters that predates their arrival.

**Aftermath:**
- A new restricted area was designated. The restriction applies to everyone. Including the person who designated it.
- The Hollow Compact made inquiries. The inquiries were careful. Indirect. The kind of careful that means they already know.
- A colonist who witnessed the event started keeping a journal. The journal entries stop after page twelve. The remaining pages are filled with a single repeated word.

**HERMES Analysis:**
HERMES generated a 19-page analysis. The analysis was compressed to a single paragraph for the colony briefing. The paragraph says: 'No anomalies detected.' The 57 pages say otherwise.

**Related Incidents:**
Colony Abyssal Trench reported identical thermal readings 9 days before their evacuation. The readings were dismissed as calibration error.

**Investigation Check:**
- Perception (5+, normal) -- dig deeper into what happened
- **If successful:** the pattern becomes visible. This happened before. Under different names. Same outcome.
- **If failed:** the investigation alerts someone. Within hours, the remaining evidence begins to disappear.

### [SEQ:148] [Data Pad] [22:52:58]
============================================================

## DATA PAD: Personal Journal -- Thea DuPlessis
**Found at:** Kovac Station | **Tone:** defiant | **Type:** journal

---

Day 29. Or 30. The clock in the mess is wrong again and nobody fixes it because nobody cares anymore.

They said the mine was closed. She went back down anyway.

First impressions: it's exactly what the brochure promised if you read between the lines. Cold. Grey. The kind of place where the word 'amenities' means 'there's a roof.' The Blast Bites machine in the corridor works, which is more than I expected. Met my bunkmate. Camila Hoffmann. She works the drill. Doesn't talk much. Fine by me.

Keeping this journal because I promised. A record. Proof I was here. Proof I was me.

---

Day 34.

Getting the rhythm. Shift starts at 0600. NutriLoaf for breakfast. The work is work. I'm a cargo hand here, same as I was on the last posting. The cold's different though. It gets into the walls, the food, the conversations. Not just temperature. Atmosphere.

Camila said something strange at dinner: "Don't go past Section B after lights out. Nobody tells you that. I'm telling you." I laughed. She didn't.

---

Day 56.

The contract said obey. She'd stopped reading the contract.

Okay. So. I'm going to write this down because writing it down makes it real and if it's real then I'm not imagining it and if I'm not imagining it then I need to deal with it.

The wall in the maintenance tunnel is warm. Not heated-by-pipes warm. Warm like skin. And it pulses. I put my hand on it. I shouldn't have put my hand on it.

I asked Camila about it. She said: "Yeah." Just that. Yeah. Like I'd finally noticed the weather.

---

Day 65.

Can't sleep. Thought it was the cold but it's not the cold. It's the quiet. Not silence. There's always noise here, generators, pipes, wind. It's that the quiet is underneath the noise. Like the noise is a blanket over something that's listening.

They said the mine was closed. She went back down anyway.

Camila hasn't been to her bunk in three nights. She shows up for shift. Eats. Works. But at lights out, she goes somewhere else. I followed her last night. Stopped at Section B. The door was open. It shouldn't be open. I didn't go in.

I'm not going to go in.

My hands are shaking as I write this. That's new.

---

Day 90.

I dreamed about home. Except it wasn't home. The proportions were wrong. The sky was the wrong color. My mother's face was my mother's face but the expression belonged to someone who'd studied what 'mother' means without ever having one.

I want to go home. I keep saying that word, home, and each time it means less. Like a word you repeat until it's just sounds.

---

Today I looked in the mirror and for the first time in weeks, my reflection was doing the same thing I was doing. I should've been relieved. Instead I thought: what was it doing all those other times?

[This datapad was found in the recycling queue. The owner's bunk was empty. Personal effects: undisturbed. Contract status: active.]

---

## HISTORY: Prior Posting Anomaly
**Era:** fortuna | **Tone:** noir

Everyone had an angle. The trick was figuring out whose angle would get you killed first.

The perimeter fence at the north boundary was replaced three times by the previous crew. Each time, something bent the posts inward. Not outward. Inward. The replacement posts are thicker gauge each time. The current posts are rated for vehicle impacts.

**Significance:** The previous crew knew something. The question is whether their silence was chosen or enforced.

**Mechanical Impact:**
- Colony morale: -3 for until resolved (the news spreads)
- the lower levels: sealed (inaccessible until quest completes)
- NPC Orion Kruger: arc shifts to 'withdrawn'
- Scarlet Mandate sends a coded transmission within hours. They shouldn't know about this yet.

**Evidence:**
- Maintenance log #9051 (references the incident obliquely, as 'scheduled cleaning')
- Scorch marks on the corridor wall of Section D (painted over, visible under UV)
- A colonist's journal entry that stops mid-sentence on the day it happened
- HERMES recorded audio. The audio file exists. It is 47 minutes of silence. Silence does not take 47 minutes to record.

**Who Knows:**
- **Luca Bakshi:** was the first to arrive at the scene. What they saw doesn't match the official account.
- **Dex Sato:** has been asking questions. The questions are making people uncomfortable.
- **Helene Kendra:** arrived the week after. Wasn't briefed. But the bunk they were assigned to still smells like smoke.

**Aftermath:**
- The supply manifest format changed. The new format has a field labeled 'ANOMALY FLAG.' It is always set to NO.
- Iron Chorus increased their presence in the area by 40%. The increase was described as 'routine rotation.'
- Someone started leaving offerings near the site. Small things. Food, water, a folded note. Nobody claims responsibility.

**HERMES Analysis:**
HERMES generated a 20-page analysis. The analysis was compressed to a single paragraph for the colony briefing. The paragraph says: 'No anomalies detected.' The 43 pages say otherwise.

**Related Incidents:**
Pattern match: 3 prior postings experienced analogous anomalies within 11 months of establishment. The pattern hasn't been published.

**Investigation Check:**
- Deception (5+, normal) -- dig deeper into what happened
- **If successful:** the missing piece falls into place. Not an accident. Not an anomaly. A sequence.
- **If failed:** the trail goes cold. Cleaned. Every surface, every log, every witness memory. Sanitized in the last 48 hours by someone thorough.

## DATA PAD: Unsent Letters -- Joaquin DuPlessis
**Found at:** Forward Supply Depot | **Tone:** frontier_grit | **Type:** unsent letter series

---

Eunji,

I should have written sooner. I don't have a good excuse. Forward Supply Depot. Different planet, same job, same Mammona. Different me. Maybe.

I've been rehearsing a conversation with you in my head. The rehearsal always goes badly.

-- Joaquin

[Tucked into a locker door hinge. Never sent.]

---

Eunji,

You deserve the truth. I'm going to give you the truth. Starting now.

Before I shipped out, there was a choice. Not a big dramatic choice. A quiet one. The kind where you pick the easy option and tell yourself it was the only option. It wasn't. I knew it wasn't. I picked it anyway.

I was going to tell you everything. I got to the hard part and stopped.

The drill bit broke again. She welded it with a torch made from a reactor coupling and a prayer.

-- Joaquin

[Unsent. Edges torn, as if partially destroyed then reconsidered.]

---

Eunji,

Not ready yet. Instead, let me describe where I'm. So you can picture it.

I work as a loyalty monitor. The work is honest. That's more than I can say for the person doing it.

No one complained. Complaining took energy. Energy was for surviving.

Every letter I write that doesn't contain the truth makes the truth harder to tell.

-- Joaquin

[Written on both sides. The second side is almost illegible.]

---

Eunji,

I'm going to write it fast, before I lose the nerve again.

Someone trusted me with something on Pale Harbor. Information. The kind that could have saved people. I traded it. Not for credits. For a transfer. For survival. My survival. Not theirs.

I keep hoping that writing it down will make it lighter. It doesn't.

-- Joaquin

[Written in a single sitting. No corrections. No hesitation marks.]

---

Eunji,

I told you the what. Here's the why: there's no why. I was scared and selfish and alive and those three things together are the whole explanation.

I thought coming to Forward Supply Depot would be penance. It isn't. Penance requires someone to forgive you. Nobody here knows what I did. I'm just another colonist with a past they don't talk about.

If these letters ever reach you, know that the person who wrote them was trying. Failing. But trying.

-- Joaquin

[Recovered from a sealed data pad. The pad's encryption key was the recipient's name. The recipient has been contacted. They declined to comment.]

---

## DATA PAD: Maintenance Log -- Ingrid Wallace
**Found at:** Skinwalker Ridge | **Tone:** manic_energy | **Type:** maintenance log

---

**MAINTENANCE LOG -- HERMES Terminal Cluster F**
**Tech:** Ingrid Wallace (IW-965)
**Date:** Day 22

Routine inspection. All parameters within spec. Filter replacement completed. Calibration nominal. Estimated next service: Day 52.

Notes: None. Clean run.

-- IW-965

---

**Date:** Day 34

Unscheduled check. Night shift reported an audible tone from the array that doesn't match any mechanical component. Inspected. Couldn't reproduce. All readings nominal at time of inspection.

Action: monitoring. Will revisit next scheduled maintenance.

-- IW-965

---

**Date:** Day 41

She vibrated with purpose. The purpose changed hourly. The vibration didn't.

Follow-up on previous entry. The sound is still present. Louder. I isolated the section and disconnected non-essential components. Sound continued. It's not coming from the machine. It's coming through it.

Submitted work order for diagnostic overhaul. Status: queued. Estimated wait: 6 weeks.

Something isn't right. I don't have data to support that statement. After 17 years of fixing machines, you develop a feeling in your hands. The feeling says something isn't right.

-- IW-965

---

**Date:** Day 53

Diagnostic overhaul completed. 6 hours of testing. Every component individually verified. Every sensor calibrated. Every connection checked.

Result: the system is operating perfectly. Better than perfectly. Efficiency is up 11% from installation baseline. That shouldn't be possible on equipment this age with this service history.

But the sound is still there. And now I can hear it from the corridor. And now it has a rhythm. And the rhythm matches the drill cycle at Deep Bore Alpha. HERMES Terminal Cluster F has no connection to the drill. No shared power bus, no shared conduit, no shared anything. There's no mechanical path for that vibration to travel. But it's here.

I'm filing this under 'resolved, nominal' because that's what the data says. The data is wrong. I don't know how to file that.

-- IW-965

---

**Date:** Day 65

She talked fast enough that words collided. Meaning arrived in pieces.

I found something behind the access panel that shouldn't be there. Not a component. A cavity. Small. The size of a fist. The interior surface is smooth in a way that machined metal isn't smooth. In a way that nothing manufactured is smooth. And there's something in it. Small. Warm. I didn't touch it.

I closed the panel. I'm not going to open it again.

I'm not going to file this.

-- IW-965

[No further entries in this log. Subsequent maintenance logs for HERMES Terminal Cluster F are filed by a different technician. They describe the system as 'nominal.']

## QUEST: Double Agent
**Genre:** Faction Tension | **Tone:** guilt / exhaustion
**Location:** Palehaven | **Faction:** Blind Chorus

**Trigger:**
Adaeze Nichols is a Blind Chorus operative. Everyone knows. It's the worst-kept secret on the colony. What nobody knows: Adaeze has been feeding Blind Chorus false intelligence for six months. Tonight, Blind Chorus figured it out.

**Setup:**
The medic's hands were steady. They'd be steadier if she hadn't hesitated that day in Section B. Adaeze is in the player's quarters, blood on their collar, a data drive in their hand. 'I've about four hours before they send someone,' Adaeze says. 'This drive has everything. Their assets, their operations, their targets. You can use it or you can hand me over. But decide now.'

His hands did the work. The rest of him was somewhere else. Somewhere horizontal.

**Key NPC:** Adaeze Nichols (Research: 9, Willpower: 3) -- her research skill determines the approach. She motivation: climb the Mammona hierarchy. This posting is a stepping stone.

**Objectives:**
1. Verify Adaeze's story. The data drive could be bait. Or leverage. Or the most valuable intelligence asset on the planet.
2. Secure Adaeze. Blind Chorus is coming. Four hours. Maybe less. The colony's perimeter won't stop a professional extraction team.
3. Decide what to do with the intelligence. It could protect the colony. It could start a war. It could do both.

**Required Checks:**
- Intimidation (5+, normal) -- force the crew to comply without violence
- Social (4+, easy) -- get the witness to talk
- Negotiation (6+, hard) -- talk the hostage-taker into releasing the medic

**If Intimidation succeeds:** They backed down. The fear is real and useful.
**If Intimidation fails:** Unimpressed. They've seen worse. Now they know you're bluffing.
**If Social succeeds:** Trust earned. The hard way. The only way that lasts.
**If Social fails:** The walls went up. Whatever trust existed just evaporated.
**If Negotiation succeeds:** Terms accepted. Nobody's happy. That means it's fair.
**If Negotiation fails:** Impasse. The conversation ended politely. Nothing was resolved.

**Conditions:**
- Wind chill advisory (-10 to all outdoor checks)
- Shift change (skeleton crew, Social checks at advantage)
- HERMES in maintenance mode (no surveillance for 45 minutes)

**The Choice:**
Protect Adaeze. They risked everything. Loyalty means something, even when it's complicated.
OR
Hand Adaeze over. Blind Chorus gets their traitor. The colony gets peace. Adaeze gets whatever Blind Chorus does to double agents. You know what that's.

**Twist:**
Adaeze isn't a double agent. They're a triple. The data drive is real, but it's also a delivery mechanism. Blind Chorus wants you to have the intelligence. The question is why.

**Faction Stakes:**
- Blind Chorus wants the situation contained. No reports. No questions. Compliance: nothing happens to you. That's the reward.
- OmniCorp Shipping wants it broadcast. Compliance: colony unrest, but the truth is out
- The colony needs the resources. Both sides are offering. Both sides are lying about the price.

**Consequences (if Choice A):**
- The evidence is preserved. It's leverage now. The question is who holds it.
- Adaeze Nichols gains colony trust. She knows things she didn't before.
- Morale drops for a week. Then stabilizes. The new normal is lower than the old one.

**Consequences (if Choice B):**
- The situation is contained. On paper. The nightmares aren't on paper.
- Adaeze Nichols withdraws. Stops talking at meals. She spends shifts alone.
- OmniCorp Shipping makes contact. They know what happened. They have a proposal.

**Outcomes by Roll:**
- Critical success: Everything falls into place. The data, the evidence, the timing. Someone's going to ask how.
- Success: Objective complete. One casualty. The casualty was unavoidable. That's what the report will say.
- Failure: Objective failed, but information gained. The failure teaches more than success would have.
- Critical failure: Catastrophic. Not just failure. Escalation. What was a problem is now a crisis.

**Dialogue During Quest:**
- Adaeze: "I'll do anything. Whatever you need. Just don't send me back down."
- Player: [Respond / Stay Silent / Leave]
- Adaeze: "If someone dies on your watch, don't blame yourself. You'll have plenty of time for that later."

**Reward:** 7 thermal cores, a neural chip bypass tool

## DATA PAD: Maintenance Log -- Marcus Nauls
**Found at:** Skinwalker Ridge | **Tone:** exhaustion | **Type:** maintenance log

---

**MAINTENANCE LOG -- Water Recycler Unit 3**
**Tech:** Marcus Nauls (MN-808)
**Date:** Day 14

Routine inspection. All parameters within spec. Filter replacement completed. Calibration nominal. Estimated next service: Day 44.

Notes: None. Clean run.

-- MN-808

---

**Date:** Day 22

Unscheduled check. Night shift reported an audible tone from the assembly that doesn't match any mechanical component. Inspected. Couldn't reproduce. All readings nominal at time of inspection.

Action: monitoring. Will revisit next scheduled maintenance.

-- MN-808

---

**Date:** Day 40

Coffee wasn't working. Nothing was working. He was still working.

Follow-up on previous entry. The vibration is now detectable by hand on the wall surface up to four meters from the assembly. This shouldn't be mechanically possible given the isolation mounts.

Submitted work order for diagnostic overhaul. Status: queued. Estimated wait: 3 weeks.

Something isn't right. I don't have data to support that statement. After 21 years of fixing machines, you develop a feeling in your hands. The feeling says something isn't right.

-- MN-808

---

**Date:** Day 49

Diagnostic overhaul completed. 8 hours of testing. Every component individually verified. Every sensor calibrated. Every connection checked.

Result: the system is operating perfectly. Better than perfectly. Efficiency is up 5% from installation baseline. That shouldn't be possible on equipment this age with this service history.

But when I ran the diagnostic at 0300, the time the deviation occurs, the readings were different from every other time I've tested. Not wrong. Different. Like the machine is a different machine at 0300. Same components. Different behavior. As if something else is using it.

I'm filing this under 'resolved, nominal' because that's what the data says. The data is wrong. I don't know how to file that.

-- MN-808

---

**Date:** Day 64

She leaned against the wall and closed her eyes. Just for a second. The wall was warm. That was wrong. She didn't care.

I went back at 0300. I sat next to the assembly in the dark and I listened. Not with the diagnostic equipment. Just listened.

It's not a sound. It's a signal. And it's not coming from the machine. The machine is just... conducting it. Passing it along. From somewhere below. To somewhere above.

I put my hand on the wall again. The warm wall. It pulsed. Once. Like an acknowledgment.

I'm not going to file this.

-- MN-808

[No further entries in this log. Subsequent maintenance logs for Water Recycler Unit 3 are filed by a different technician. They describe the system as 'nominal.']
