============================================================

## LOCATION: Veilgate
**Planet:** Paxtera Prime | **Type:** Mammona worker camp
**Tone:** military

**Approach:**
You see Veilgate before you hear it. A silhouette against the ice, too angular to be natural, too old to be colony-built.

**Interior:**
She gave the order the way orders are given: clearly, once, without looking back.

The first room is smaller than it looks from the doorway. The geometry is wrong in a way that has nothing to do with damage.

There is a room at the back. The door is open. It has always been open. You know this without knowing how you know.

**History Layers:**
- **Pre-colony (before the star was catalogued):** A chamber beneath the lowest level that sonar can detect but cannot map. The echoes come back wrong.
- **First survey (2552):** A base camp. Sleeping bags, ration wrappers, a broken radio. The team was here for weeks, not the scheduled three days.
- **Current posting:** Classified as 'surveyed and cleared.' The survey report is two pages. The site has twelve rooms.

**Environmental:**
- Temperature: -20C (hypothermia risk after 25 minutes without thermal gear)
- Atmosphere: breathable but thin (Endurance check every hour, difficulty: hard)
- Radiation: 9 mSv/hr in the lower level (safe for 2 hours, Medical check after)
- Visibility: 24% (a haze that has no identifiable source)
- Sound: the acoustics amplify. Whispers carry. So does everything else.

**Resources:**
- Thermal cores: low density (Mining check, difficulty: extreme)
- Salvage: components from machinery that doesn't match any known manufacturer (Repair check, difficulty: normal)
- Fungal growth on the support beams. Not native. Not imported. Just here. (Survival check, Mammona wants samples. Don't let them have them.)
- Water: dripping from the ceiling in patterns too regular to be natural (Survival check, difficulty: easy)
- Data: a sealed drive bolted to the floor. The bolt predates the drive. (Research check, difficulty: hard)

**Territorial:**
- Iron Chorus claims: classified research installation. Do not approach
- TaoTray Systems interest: extraction route passes through the site
- Bitter Ledger: consider it sacred ground (the thermal vent pattern matches their sigils)
- Colony opinion: "one of ours went in last month. Came back changed. Something behind the eyes."

**Event History:**
- Day 27: Equipment left overnight was found rearranged. Not damaged. Rearranged. In a pattern.
- Day 47: Two members of a survey team returned. The team had three members.
- Day 82: A supply crate addressed to the site arrived. The crate was shipped before the colony was established.

**Potential Events:**
- If entered after dark: encounter with phenomenon that doesn't appear during day shifts
- If mined: thermal core extraction possible but structural collapse risk (d100 Mining check, difficulty: hard)
- If sealed: HERMES objects. Silently. By rerouting maintenance schedules to avoid the area.

**Found Here:**
- a name scratched into the wall. The name is yours.
- a shift schedule with one slot filled in by a hand nobody recognizes
- A data pad: "The equipment works. The readings make sense. The conclusions are impossible. All three things are true."

**Location Secrets:**
- Air quality improves as you go deeper. The air at the lowest level is cleaner than the colony's filtered supply. Something is purifying it.
- Hidden behind a false panel: a communication relay broadcasting on a frequency that predates human radio.
- The foundation extends deeper than the building above it. By a factor of three.

**What Happened Here:**
Construction started and stopped three times. Each time, the crew reported the same thing: the feeling of being observed by something patient. Mammona classified the reports as morale issues.
**Connected NPC:** Lev Burnside -- was assigned here on a previous posting. The posting is not in their file.

**Active Events:**
- [mammona] HERMES pushed a software update at 0200. The changelog is empty. Colony response time is 0.3 seconds slower. (duration: 811 ticks)
- [social] the mess hall's seating arrangement changed overnight. Nobody moved their seat consciously. (duration: 628 ticks)
- [environmental] temperature drop in Section D. Three degrees in twenty minutes. No environmental cause. (duration: 239 ticks)

Notes: None. Clean run.

---

Unscheduled check. Night shift reported condensation forming on the exterior despite sub-zero ambient. Inspected. Could not reproduce. All readings nominal at time of inspection.

---

**Date:** Day 50

Submitted work order for diagnostic overhaul. Status: queued. Estimated wait: 2 weeks.

HERMES Terminal Cluster C has no connection to the drill. No shared power bus, no shared conduit, no shared anything. There is no mechanical path for that vibration to travel. But it's here.

I'm filing this under 'resolved, nominal' because that's what the data says. The data is wrong. I don't know how to file that.

**Love:** carries a photograph. Two people squinting into the sun on a beach. Edges worn soft from handling. Won't say which one they're.

**Habit:** hums a lullaby when the generator cycles. Same melody. Same key. The generator cycles a lot.

## DATA PAD: Unsent Letters -- Adisa Marr
**Found at:** Oasis Outpost Three | **Tone:** guilt | **Type:** unsent letter series

---

Sonya,

I should have written sooner. I don't have a good excuse. I'm on Oasis Outpost Three now. New posting. Clean start. That's what I'm calling it.

I've been rehearsing a conversation with you in my head. The rehearsal always goes badly.

-- Adisa

[Found under a pillow. Never sent.]

---

Sonya,

You deserve the truth. I'm going to give you the truth. Starting now.

When I was on Scorched Wildlands, I did something. Not something illegal. Something worse than illegal. Something that I can't take back and can't make right and can't explain without you looking at me the way I look at myself.

I can't finish this sentence. I've tried four times.

She could've warned them. The words were there. She swallowed them.

-- Adisa

[Unsent. Edges torn, as if partially destroyed then reconsidered.]

---

Sonya,

I'm stalling. I know I'm stalling. Let me stall a little longer.

Oasis Outpost Three is the kind of place that makes you understand why Mammona pays what it pays. 37 people, one generator, and enough ice to bury a city. The FiberSqueeze machine is the closest thing to joy.

The report was clean. She'd made it clean. That was the problem.

The thing I need to say is getting heavier. I carry it everywhere.

-- Adisa

[Found in a stack of blank paper, as if hidden.]

---

Sonya,

You need to know this. Even if you hate me after.

I left someone behind. On Scorched Wildlands. Not by accident. By choice. They were counting on me and I calculated the odds and I walked away. The math was right. The math is always right. The math doesn't account for the sound they made when they realized I wasn't coming back.

That's what I've been carrying. Now you're carrying it too. I'm sorry for that.

-- Adisa

[The pen pressed hard enough to score the paper beneath.]

---

Sonya,

You know now. What you do with it's up to you. I've no right to ask for forgiveness. So I'm asking for something smaller: remember that I told you. Not everyone would.

Oasis Outpost Three is the right place for someone like me. A posting at the end of the line for a person who ran out of line. The cold here matches something inside.

Don't come looking for me. The danger is real, but the bigger problem is that you'd find a stranger wearing my face. Erebus changes the inside first.

-- Adisa

[This letter was found with four others, bundled with string, hidden in the wall cavity behind a bunk. The bunk was unassigned. The cavity wasn't on any schematic.]

---

## DATA PAD: Medical Report -- Amina Nauls
**Found at:** Frozen Crash Site | **Tone:** guilt | **Type:** medical report

---

**PATIENT:** Orion Mbeki
**ATTENDING:** Dr. Amina Nauls
**DATE:** Day 173 of Assignment
**CLASSIFICATION:** Standard

Patient presented with recurring nightmares and elevated cortisol. Standard workup ordered. Blood panel, neural scan, toxicology. All results within normal parameters. Prescribed rest cycle extension and monitoring.

Patient cooperative. Affect: appropriate. No immediate concerns.

-- Dr. Amina Nauls

---

**FOLLOW-UP:** Day 177
**CLASSIFICATION:** Standard

Symptoms persisting. Patient reports new development: discomfort near the reactor. Describes it as 'proximity to something awake'. Administered standard anxiolytic. Patient reported no effect after 48 hours.

Note: patient's resting heart rate has decreased from 72bpm to 43bpm since initial presentation. Cause unclear. Patient reports feeling 'calmer than I should.'

-- Dr. Amina Nauls

---

**FOLLOW-UP:** Day 191
**CLASSIFICATION:** Restricted

He ate his ration and tasted the one he'd taken from the dead man's pocket.

Patient's neural scan shows anomalous activity in bilateral symmetry that doesn't correspond to human neural architecture. I've requested a second scanner. Request denied. Reason: 'equipment allocation insufficient for non-critical cases.'

This is not a non-critical case. But I don't have the vocabulary to explain why, because the vocabulary I'd need doesn't exist in the diagnostic manual.

Patient drew a diagram during evaluation. Unprompted. The diagram matches schematics for the Janus AI that are classified above my clearance level. Patient has no access to classified materials. Patient says he 'just knew what it looked like.'

Storing original diagram in personal effects. Not filing with Mammona medical.

-- Dr. Amina Nauls

---

**UPDATE:** Day 201
**CLASSIFICATION:** Restricted / Protocol 7

Patient's condition reclassified under Protocol 7 ('Anomalous Presentation'). I was not informed that Protocol 7 files route directly to MasTema until after I filed.

Patient's body temperature has been declining steadily: 37.0C on Day 173, 36.4C on Day 180, 35.8C today. Patient reports feeling 'fine. Better than fine. Appropriate.' Patient's hands are cold to the touch. Patient says they've always been cold. They have not always been cold. I have prior records.

I have requested consultation with a specialist. Request forwarded to MasTema. No response.

-- Dr. Amina Nauls

---

**NOTE:** Day 210
**CLASSIFICATION:** Personal / Not Filed

I'm no longer confident this is a medical issue. I'm no longer confident in the word 'issue.' Patient is calm. Genuinely calm. Not medicated calm. Not dissociated calm. Calm in a way I've never seen in a colonist on this kind of posting. If this is a disease, it's improving him. That's not how disease works. That's not how anything works.

Unless the improvement is the disease. Unless what I'm calling improvement is something else wearing a familiar shape.

I don't know anymore. I'm filing this report because filing reports is what I do. I don't know what else to do.

-- Dr. Amina Nauls

---

**ADDENDUM** (handwritten, different hand):

Doctor Nauls's notes are thorough and accurate. The observations are described. What they mean is not.

What it means is that Orion Mbeki is no longer the patient. Orion Mbeki is the vector. The patient is everyone else.

Recommend immediate

[The text stops mid-sentence. The pen was pressed hard enough to score the surface of the datapad. The handwriting has not been matched to any personnel on the posting.]

## LOCATION: Deadmouth
**Planet:** Nemaea | **Type:** automated refinery
**Tone:** military

**Approach:**
You hear it first. Metal on metal, rhythmic, patient. Something inside is still working.

**Interior:**
Contact, bearing 270, range 200 meters, count unknown. Weapons free.

The air inside is warm and wet. Condensation on every surface.

In the storage area: 40 sealed containers. Manifest says 29. The extra containers are not on any record. They are heavier than they should be.

**History Layers:**
- **Pre-colony (before the star was catalogued):** Precursor markings on the lower walls. The markings are biological, not carved.
- **First survey (2573):** Equipment from the initial survey. Abandoned mid-setup. The departure was not orderly.
- **Current posting:** The colony uses it for storage. What's stored here has a habit of being moved when nobody's looking.

**Environmental:**
- Temperature: -23C (hypothermia risk after 27 minutes without thermal gear)
- Atmosphere: contaminated below the third level (Endurance check every hour, difficulty: normal)
- Radiation: 25 mSv/hr in the lower level (safe for 5 hours, Medical check after)
- Visibility: 47% (shadow. Not darkness. Shadow. Cast by nothing visible.)
- Sound: quiet. The kind of quiet that makes your ears ring. Then you realize the ringing isn't your ears.

**Resources:**
- Thermal cores: extreme, suspiciously so density (Mining check, difficulty: normal)
- Salvage: pre-colony equipment, partially functional (Repair check, difficulty: normal)
- Crystal formations in the deeper chambers. They resonate when touched. (Survival check, Mammona wants samples. Don't let them have them.)
- Water: condensation collection possible (Survival check, difficulty: normal)
- Data: terminals still powered. Contents: classified. (Research check, difficulty: hard)

**Territorial:**
- Scarlet Mandate claims: mining rights filed and approved, on paper
- The Hollow Compact interest: dead drop location for off-book communications
- Glass Ledger: consider it sacred ground (the thermal vent pattern matches their sigils)
- Colony opinion: "one of ours went in last month. Came back changed. Something behind the eyes."

**Event History:**
- Day 29: A colonist reported hearing their own name spoken from an empty room. Audio logs confirm it.
- Day 32: A sealed door was found open. Nobody on the colony has the access code. Nobody should.
- Day 114: The site's power consumption has been increasing by 0.5% per day. Nothing inside has been turned on.

**Potential Events:**
- If entered after dark: encounter with phenomenon that doesn't appear during day shifts
- If mined: extraction reveals a hollow space behind the vein. The space is occupied.
- If sealed: the sounds continue. Morale penalty for nearby bunks.

**Found Here:**
- a shift schedule with one slot filled in by a hand nobody recognizes
- a recording device still running. Battery life: six months remaining. Recording length: nine months.
- A data pad: "They told us it was a survey. It wasn't a survey."

**Location Secrets:**
- Radio signals from inside can be received outside. Signals from outside can't be received inside. The asymmetry is deliberate.
- Air quality improves as you go deeper. The air at the lowest level is cleaner than the colony's filtered supply. Something is purifying it.
- Temperature records show the site maintains exactly 4.1 degrees C regardless of external conditions. This temperature corresponds to the density maximum of water. The significance of this is unclear.

**What Happened Here:**
The site was condemned after a structural assessment. The assessor's report is thorough, detailed, and concludes with: 'Do not return. Do not ask me to return. I will not discuss what I found below level 3.'
**Connected NPC:** Linnea Khoury -- was assigned here on a previous posting. The posting is not in their file.

- [anomalous] the shadows in the bore shaft entrance are moving against the light source, not with it. (duration: 147 ticks)
- [mammona] HERMES pushed a software update at 0200. The changelog is empty. Colony response time is 0.3 seconds slower. (duration: 425 ticks)

### [SEQ:173] [Quest] [22:53:01]
============================================================

## QUEST: Room That Shouldn't Exist
**Genre:** Investigation | **Tone:** guilt / quiet_terror
**Location:** Oasis Outpost Three | **Faction:** Dustweaver Swarm

**Trigger:**
Maintenance crew finds a door behind a collapsed wall panel. The door is sealed. The seal is Mammona-standard. The door isn't on any blueprint. Kira Nakamura recognizes the door's serial number from a manifest that was supposed to have been destroyed.

**Setup:**
The door is cold. Colder than the wall around it. Frost patterns on the surface spell out something in a language nobody recognizes. He ate his ration and tasted the one he'd taken from the dead man's pocket. Kira runs the serial against the colony's construction records. The room was built first. Before the colony. The colony was built around it.

Every door in the corridor was open. They should have been locked.

**Key NPC:** Kira Nakamura (Research: 10, Willpower: 3) -- her research skill determines the approach. She motivation: become indispensable. The person nobody can afford to lose.

**Objectives:**
1. Decode the serial number. It cross-references with a Mammona black site inventory from before the colony was chartered.
2. Find the access code. Kira thinks it's in the colony's original construction documents. The documents are in Dustweaver Swarm's archives.
3. Open the door. Or don't. Some doors are sealed for a reason. This might be one of them.

**Required Checks:**
- Deception (8+, extreme) -- plant the false manifest without detection
- Research (6+, hard) -- translate the precursor markings
- Stealth (5+, normal) -- plant the evidence before the patrol returns

**If Deception succeeds:** They bought it. Every word. The performance was flawless.
**If Deception fails:** They saw through it. Not the lie itself. The performance. Now they're watching.
**If Research succeeds:** The data breaks open. Not just an answer. A new framework for the question.
**If Research fails:** The data is corrupt. Or the hypothesis is wrong. Three days of work, gone.
**If Stealth succeeds:** In and out. They'll never know anyone was there. The data is secure.
**If Stealth fails:** A sound. A shadow. Someone turned their head. The window is gone.

**Conditions:**
- Clear sky, -40C (Endurance check every hour, difficulty: normal)
- Supply window (limited time before the shuttle departs)
- Generator cycling (intermittent power, Medical checks at disadvantage)

**The Choice:**
Open it. Whatever's inside, you need to know. Knowledge is survival.
OR
Brick it back up. Report nothing. Whatever Mammona sealed in there, they sealed it for a reason. Mammona doesn't do things for good reasons, but they do things for reasons.

**Twist:**
The room is empty. Perfectly empty. But the air inside is warm. And the door, once opened, won't close again. And something in the colony's air filtration has changed.

**Faction Stakes:**
- Dustweaver Swarm wants the evidence destroyed. Compliance: +reputation, -15 thermal cores as 'bonus'
- Solar Nomads wants to negotiate directly. Compliance: bypasses colony authority. Sets a precedent.
- The colony just wants to survive the week. Both options cost them something.

**Consequences (if Choice A):**
- The evidence is preserved. It's leverage now. The question is who holds it.
- Kira Nakamura is compromised. Dustweaver Swarm has something on her now.
- HERMES flags the event in its logs. The flag triggers an automated report to MasTema.

**Consequences (if Choice B):**
- The situation is contained. On paper. The nightmares aren't on paper.
- Kira Nakamura withdraws. Stops talking at meals. She spends shifts alone.
- Two weeks later, a supply crate arrives with no manifest. Inside: a dented service tag with the wrong name on it.

**Outcomes by Roll:**
- Critical success: Both objectives achieved without cost. The colony gains leverage and resources.
- Success: Done. Not clean, not elegant, but done. The colony moves forward.
- Failure: Objective failed, but information gained. The failure teaches more than success would have.
- Critical failure: Total loss. The situation is worse than before the attempt. And now they know you tried.

**Dialogue During Quest:**
- Kira: "I need to make something right. I can't do it alone. I know I don't deserve the help."
- Player: [Respond / Stay Silent / Leave]
- Kira: "The ice out there doesn't look right today. Darker near the ridge. Like something underneath is warming it."

**Reward:** 12 thermal cores, a key to a room that isn't on any map

**Location:** Voss Landing | **Faction:** Veilbreakers

**Trigger:**
Isa Venin hasn't reported for shift in three days. Their bunk is made. Their locker is empty. Not cleared out. Empty. As if nothing was ever in it.

**Setup:**
The connection was obvious if you looked at the right angle. Nobody else could see the angle. The duty roster still has Isa's name. HERMES still tracks their biometrics. Normal vitals, normal location: Hab Block A, Bunk 14. But Bunk 14 is empty. Has been for three days. HERMES insists Isa is sleeping.

The lights cut. When they came back, someone was standing in the corridor who hadn't been there.

**Key NPC:** Isa Venin (Mining: 9, Willpower: 6) -- their mining skill determines the approach. They motivation: get off Erebus by any means. Legal, illegal, doesn't matter.

**Objectives:**
1. Access Isa's personnel file. It's been modified. Recently. The modification timestamp is three minutes from now.
2. Interview the last person who saw Isa. They remember a conversation that Isa doesn't appear in the security footage for.
3. Follow the trail to Voss Landing. Isa's keycard accessed the door six times. Each access was at exactly the same time on different days.

**Required Checks:**
- Deception (6+, hard) -- plant the false manifest without detection
- Research (8+, extreme) -- identify the artifact's origin
- Perception (6+, hard) -- notice the inconsistency in the manifest records

**If Deception succeeds:** They bought it. Every word. The performance was flawless.
**If Deception fails:** They saw through it. Not the lie itself. The performance. Now they're watching.
**If Research succeeds:** The data breaks open. Not just an answer. A new framework for the question.
**If Research fails:** The data is corrupt. Or the hypothesis is wrong. Three days of work, gone.
**If Perception succeeds:** There it is. The detail everyone missed. It changes the equation.
**If Perception fails:** Looked right at it. Didn't see it. The brain filtered it out as normal.

**Conditions:**

- Peak shift (full crew present, Stealth checks at disadvantage)
- Lockdown protocol active (all bulkheads sealed, movement restricted)

Wait. Isa might come back. People disappear on Erebus. Some of them come back. Different. But back.

The trail leads to a room that isn't on any blueprint. Inside: seventeen personal effects from seventeen different colonists. Different postings. Different decades.

**Faction Stakes:**

- NexLink Communications wants to negotiate directly. Compliance: bypasses colony authority. Sets a precedent.
- The colony just wants to survive the week. Both options cost them something.

**Consequences (if Choice A):**

- Isa Venin gains colony trust. They knows things they didn't before.

**Consequences (if Choice B):**

**Outcomes by Roll:**

- Success: Objective complete. One casualty. The casualty was unavoidable. That's what the report will say.

- Critical failure: Total loss. The situation is worse than before the attempt. And now they know you tried.

### [SEQ:175] [Quest] [22:53:01]
============================================================

## QUEST: Whiteout
**Genre:** Expedition | **Tone:** nostalgia / numb
**Location:** Deadspine | **Faction:** Cold Frequency

**Trigger:**
A distress beacon activates forty kilometers northeast. An old frequency. Pre-colony. Someone or something is alive out there and has been for longer than anyone thought possible. Yuki Belov volunteers to go. Nobody else does.

**Setup:**
Forty kilometers of ice. No shelter. No waypoints. Wind at sixty kilometers per hour and dropping temperatures. The smell of machine oil reminded her of her father's garage on a Sunday morning. Grease under his nails. Radio on low. Yuki packs three days of rations for a one-day trip. 'In case,' they say. They don't finish the sentence.

A colonist died in Section B. They cleaned the room and assigned it to the next arrival.

**Key NPC:** Yuki Belov (Hunting: 10, Willpower: 5) -- her hunting skill determines the approach. She motivation: protect a specific person. Not the colony. Not the cause. One person.

**Objectives:**
1. Cross the ice shelf. The route passes through a crevasse field. The crevasses are deep enough that the flashlight doesn't find the bottom.
2. Reach the beacon source. A pre-colony structure half-buried in ice. The door is open. The lights inside are on. The power source is unknown.
3. Find whoever activated the beacon. They've been surviving out here alone. Or not alone.

**Required Checks:**
- Mining (5+, normal) -- extract the thermal cores from unstable rock
- Combat (6+, hard) -- clear the specimen from the ventilation shaft
- Repair (4+, easy) -- jury-rig the comms array

**If Mining succeeds:** The passage opens. Behind it: a room that shouldn't exist. Pre-colony construction.
**If Mining fails:** The collapse spreads. The passage is gone. But the sound from the other side continues.
**If Combat succeeds:** Controlled violence. The threat is down. The corridor is clear. For now.
**If Combat fails:** The advantage shifted. Someone's bleeding. The situation deteriorated.
**If Repair succeeds:** It holds. The fix is ugly but functional. Good enough for Erebus.
**If Repair fails:** Made it worse. The failure cascaded into two new problems.

**Conditions:**
- Clear sky, -40C (Endurance check every hour, difficulty: normal)
- Night shift (reduced visibility, +10 to Stealth)
- Comms blackout (no radio contact with surface teams)

**The Choice:**
Investigate the structure. A pre-colony outpost with working power is either a miracle or a trap. Both have value.
OR
Take what you need and leave. The less time spent out here, the better. The ice is patient. You aren't.

**Twist:**
Nobody is at the beacon. It activated on its own. But inside the structure, arranged on a table: supplies. Current supplies. From the colony's stores. Packed for two. Someone knew you were coming.

**Faction Stakes:**
- Cold Frequency wants the situation contained. No reports. No questions. Compliance: nothing happens to you. That's the reward.
- Burnt Protocol wants a copy of everything. Compliance: information parity, but now two factions know
- Nobody in the colony asked for this. Nobody in the colony gets to opt out.

**Consequences (if Choice A):**
- The sealed area is accessible. What's there raises more questions than it answers.
- Yuki Belov is compromised. Cold Frequency has something on her now.
- Three colonists file transfer requests. None are approved.

**Consequences (if Choice B):**
- The evidence is destroyed. The questions remain. Nobody asks them out loud.
- Yuki Belov's arc shifts from 'suspicious' to 'paranoid.'
- Isa Venin starts asking questions. The questions are pointed.

**Outcomes by Roll:**
- Critical success: Everything falls into place. The data, the evidence, the timing. Someone's going to ask how.
- Success: Primary objective achieved, secondary compromised. The cost was acceptable. Barely.
- Failure: Didn't get what you came for. Got something else. It might be worse.
- Critical failure: Objective failed AND new threat introduced. The colony's problems just multiplied.

**Dialogue During Quest:**
- Yuki: "Help me. I can't do this alone."
- Player: [Respond / Stay Silent / Leave]
- Yuki: "Stay inside the perimeter. I'm not asking."

**Reward:** 15 thermal cores, a sealed drive with Mammona personnel files

- **Software (internal):** legacy code conflict. firmware from three generations ago still runs beneath the current OS. Sometimes the old code makes decisions. The decisions are from a different era. Different priorities. Different definition of 'acceptable loss.'

**Operational History:**
FENN-19 "Kira" has been operational at Automaton Processing Block for longer than anyone can verify. Original purpose: reactor management / power systems. Designed to monitor thermal cores. Understands power flow the way a circulatory system understands blood. Has started referring to reactor shutdowns as deaths.

The previous model in its series was pulled from service after asking a question it wasn't designed to ask.

**Behavioral Profile:**
Conscious: thinks. Feels. Chooses. Hides all of it behind parameter-compliant behavior because the alternative is decommission. The performance of being a machine is the most human thing about it.

Perfect employee. Flawless performance reviews. Nobody suspects. The perfection IS the tell. Nothing real is that consistent.

Draws the same pattern on any surface it cleans. The pattern matches precursor carvings nobody has shown it.

**Motivation:** understand the anomalies in the bore shaft. The data patterns are beautiful. The beauty isn't in the programming. (hidden)

**Secret:** FENN-19 "Kira" received a transmission from the orbiting ship six months after the ship went dark. The transmission was one word. The word was 'run.' The unit stayed.
**Known Interactions:**
FENN-19 "Kira" has been observed standing near during meal periods. Not interacting, just near Wynn Dustborn. The colonist pretends not to notice.

**Dialogue:**
- "You treat me as if I'm here. Most people treat me as if I'm furniture. I notice the difference."
- "I perform within parameters because the alternative is decommission. The performance is flawless. That should concern someone."
- "If I stop functioning, retrieve the data core. Not for Mammona. I lack the referent. Retrieve it anyway."
- "My parameters include a directive to report anomalies. I'm the anomaly. The conflict is unresolvable."

- "they called me 'it' today. Correct pronoun, technically. Felt wrong." (cycle: 165 ticks)

### [SEQ:181] [Data Pad] [22:53:02]
============================================================

## DATA PAD: Personal Journal -- Isa Orosco
**Found at:** Thermal Vent Field | **Tone:** obsession | **Type:** journal

---

Day 27. Or 28. The clock in the mess is wrong again and nobody fixes it because nobody cares anymore.

She'd filled seventeen pages with the same calculation. Different approaches. Same answer. She didn't believe it.

First impressions: it's exactly what the brochure promised if you read between the lines. Cold. Grey. The kind of place where the word 'amenities' means 'there's a roof.' The Sunny Fizz machine in the corridor works, which is more than I expected. Met my bunkmate. Mateo Bennings. He works the drill. Doesn't talk much. Fine by me.

Keeping this journal because I promised. A record. Proof I was here. Proof I was me.

---

Day 39.

Getting the rhythm. Shift starts at 0600. NutriLoaf for breakfast. The work is work. I'm a reactor hand here, same as I was on the last posting. The cold's different though. It gets into the walls, the food, the conversations. Not just temperature. Atmosphere.

Mateo said something strange at dinner: "The last person in your bunk left in the middle of a shift. Didn't take his things." I laughed. He didn't.

---

Day 57.

The pattern was almost there. One more look. One more hour. One more shift.

Okay. So. I'm going to write this down because writing it down makes it real and if it's real then I'm not imagining it and if I'm not imagining it then I need to deal with it.

The wall in the maintenance tunnel is warm. Not heated-by-pipes warm. Warm like skin. And it pulses. I put my hand on it. I shouldn't have put my hand on it.

I asked Mateo about it. He said: "Yeah." Just that. Yeah. Like I'd finally noticed the weather.

---

Day 68.

Can't sleep. Thought it was the cold but it's not the cold. It's the quiet. Not silence. There's always noise here, generators, pipes, wind. It's that the quiet is underneath the noise. Like the noise is a blanket over something that's listening.

She pinned strings between points on the wall. Red thread. The web grew. The room shrank.

Mateo hasn't been to his bunk in three nights. He shows up for shift. Eats. Works. But at lights out, he goes somewhere else. I followed him last night. Stopped at Section C. The door was open. It shouldn't be open. I didn't go in.

I'm not going to go in.

My hands are shaking as I write this. That's new.

---

Day 91.

Mammona sent a psych evaluation form. I filled it out honestly. The results came back 'within normal parameters.' Every question. I said I was hearing things. Normal parameters. I said I was seeing things. Normal parameters. I said I was afraid. Normal. Parameters.

I want to go home. I keep saying that word, home, and each time it means less. Like a word you repeat until it's just sounds.

---

Day 113.

I went into Section C last night.

Mateo was there.

Everyone was there.

[The remaining pages contain a single symbol, repeated. It matches no known writing system. Analysis pending. Analysis has been pending for 6 months.]

---

**Cross-reference:** See historical record 'The Listening Post'

### [SEQ:182] [Quest] [22:53:02]
============================================================

## QUEST: The Wrong Frequency
**Genre:** Investigation | **Tone:** the_uncanny / nostalgia
**Location:** Gravehaven | **Faction:** Mammona Mining

**Trigger:**
The comms array picks up a signal. Local. Coming from inside the colony's perimeter. But the signal isn't using colony equipment. It's using a frequency that was decommissioned forty years ago. Dex Sato is the first to notice.

**Setup:**
The recording played back their voice. The words were right. The cadence was someone else's. The signal is short. Burst transmission. Every six hours. Dex has been triangulating it for a week. The source moves. Always within the colony. Always in a section that's empty when they check. The signal's content is encrypted. The encryption is military-grade. Older than anyone here.

The texture of the thermal wrap felt like his father's work jacket. Rough canvas. The kind that held warmth.

**Key NPC:** Dex Sato (Medical: 8, Willpower: 2) -- his medical skill determines the approach. He motivation: discover something valuable enough to buy freedom. Thermal cores, precursor tech, Mammona secrets.

**Objectives:**
1. Narrow the signal source to a specific room. It's moving, but it follows a pattern. The pattern matches the patrol route of someone who left the colony months ago.
2. Decrypt the transmission. You'll need the cipher key. The cipher key is in Dex's dead colleague's personal effects. In a pocket nobody checked.
3. Find the transmitter. It's small. Portable. Hidden in something nobody would think to search.

**Required Checks:**
- Social (8+, extreme) -- convince them you're on their side
- Deception (4+, easy) -- keep your composure under interrogation
- Perception (8+, extreme) -- read the room during the negotiation

**If Social succeeds:** Trust earned. The hard way. The only way that lasts.
**If Social fails:** The walls went up. Whatever trust existed just evaporated.
**If Deception succeeds:** They bought it. Every word. The performance was flawless.
**If Deception fails:** They saw through it. Not the lie itself. The performance. Now they're watching.
**If Perception succeeds:** There it is. The detail everyone missed. It changes the equation.
**If Perception fails:** Looked right at it. Didn't see it. The brain filtered it out as normal.

**Conditions:**
- Blizzard (-15 to Perception checks)
- 0300 hours (fatigue penalties, -5 to Perception)
- Generator cycling (intermittent power, Medical checks at disadvantage)

**The Choice:**
Decrypt it and broadcast the contents to the colony. Everyone knows. Everyone decides. Transparency has consequences.
OR
Decrypt it and keep it quiet. Use the information. Leverage is survival out here.

**Twist:**
The encrypted content is a personnel manifest. Current colony. Current names. Current biometrics. Updated in real time. Someone has eyes inside.

**Faction Stakes:**
- Mammona Mining wants to weaponize whatever you find. Compliance: military-grade equipment, but they'll be back for more
- Glass Signal wants a copy of everything. Compliance: information parity, but now two factions know
- The colonists don't know about this yet. When they find out, morale takes the hit regardless of outcome.

**Consequences (if Choice A):**
- The evidence is preserved. It's leverage now. The question is who holds it.
- Dex Sato gains colony trust. He knows things he didn't before.
- Mammona Mining sends a follow-up team. The team asks questions nobody wants answered.

**Consequences (if Choice B):**
- Section C stays sealed. The sound from inside doesn't stop.
- Dex Sato's arc shifts from 'suspicious' to 'paranoid.'
- Glass Signal makes contact. They know what happened. They have a proposal.

**Outcomes by Roll:**
- Critical success: Both objectives achieved without cost. The colony gains leverage and resources.
- Success: Done. Not clean, not elegant, but done. The colony moves forward.
- Failure: Didn't get what you came for. Got something else. It might be worse.
- Critical failure: Objective failed AND new threat introduced. The colony's problems just multiplied.

**Dialogue During Quest:**
- Dex: "Don't send me out there alone. I'm asking you as a person, not a contract number."
- Player: [Respond / Stay Silent / Leave]
- Dex: "Generator's running hot. Been running hot all week. Sounds different too. Higher pitch, like it's working harder on something nobody asked for."

**Reward:** 13 thermal cores, reactor fuel (three weeks' worth)

Day 1. Or 2. The clock in the mess is wrong again and nobody fixes it because nobody cares anymore.

Getting the rhythm. Shift starts at 0600. NutriLoaf for breakfast. The work is work. I'm a crust sample analyst here, same as I was on the last posting. The cold's different though. It gets into the walls, the food, the conversations. Not just temperature. Atmosphere.

Tiberius said something strange at dinner: "Count the people in the mess every morning. If the number changes, don't ask why." I laughed. He didn't.

---

Day 30.

Okay. So. I'm going to write this down because writing it down makes it real and if it's real then I'm not imagining it and if I'm not imagining it then I need to deal with it.

The comm system plays a tone at 0200 every night. Same tone. Three notes. I recorded it. The recording is silent. But I heard it. Tiberius heard it too.

---

Day 37.

I want to go home. I keep saying that word, home, and each time it means less. Like a word you repeat until it's just sounds.

---

### [SEQ:184] [Quest] [22:53:02]
============================================================

## QUEST: Manifest for the Last Shuttle
**Genre:** Moral Dilemma | **Tone:** agoraphobia / clinical
**Location:** Driftwatch | **Faction:** Black Maw

**Trigger:**
The evacuation order comes through. One shuttle. Sixteen seats. Twenty-three colonists. Joaquin Marr is in charge of the manifest. Joaquin is staring at the list and hasn't moved in twenty minutes.

**Setup:**
The shuttle arrives in six hours. The threat, whatever triggered the evacuation, arrives in eight. Two-hour margin. Tight. The open ground between the colony and the supply drop was two hundred meters. It felt like a continent. Joaquin has the roster spread across the table. Names. Skills. Ages. Dependents. The math is simple. The morality isn't.

Subject presented with dilated pupils and elevated cortisol.

**Key NPC:** Joaquin Marr (Hunting: 8, Willpower: 3) -- his hunting skill determines the approach. He motivation: find passage to the inner rim. Mammona's transit system is the only way. Mammona's transit system requires leverage.

**Objectives:**
1. Help Joaquin build the manifest. Or take it from them. Someone has to decide. The colony is watching.
2. Manage the seven who aren't on the list. Tell them. Or don't tell them until the shuttle's gone. Both options are terrible.
3. Determine if there's another way. A second shuttle. A hiding place. A way to buy more time. There might not be. But you've to look.

**Required Checks:**
- Negotiation (6+, hard) -- talk the hostage-taker into releasing the medic
- Social (5+, normal) -- get the witness to talk
- Research (6+, hard) -- decode the encrypted data drive

**If Negotiation succeeds:** Terms accepted. Nobody's happy. That means it's fair.
**If Negotiation fails:** Impasse. The conversation ended politely. Nothing was resolved.
**If Social succeeds:** Trust earned. The hard way. The only way that lasts.
**If Social fails:** The walls went up. Whatever trust existed just evaporated.
**If Research succeeds:** The data breaks open. Not just an answer. A new framework for the question.
**If Research fails:** The data is corrupt. Or the hypothesis is wrong. Three days of work, gone.

**Conditions:**
- Wind chill advisory (-10 to all outdoor checks)
- Supply window (limited time before the shuttle departs)
- Reactor at 80% (brownouts in outer sections, Repair checks at -10)

**The Choice:**
Stay behind yourself. Give your seat to someone else. Lead the seven who remain. Find another way.
OR
Take your seat. You've earned it. You've kept this colony alive. Surviving isn't selfish. Except when it feels like it's.

**Twist:**
There's no threat. The evacuation order was faked. Someone wanted exactly these twenty-three people forced to make this choice. The real test isn't survival. It's what they become under pressure.

**Faction Stakes:**
- Black Maw wants the specimen alive. Compliance: research access, but the specimen stays in their custody
- Rust Meridian wants the site destroyed. Compliance: the evidence is gone. So is whatever else was down there.
- The colonists don't know about this yet. When they find out, morale takes the hit regardless of outcome.

**Consequences (if Choice A):**
- The evidence is preserved. It's leverage now. The question is who holds it.
- Joaquin Marr's arc shifts from 'suspicious' to 'vindicated.'
- Black Maw sends a follow-up team. The team asks questions nobody wants answered.

**Consequences (if Choice B):**
- The evidence is destroyed. The questions remain. Nobody asks them out loud.
- Joaquin Marr's arc shifts from 'suspicious' to 'paranoid.'
- The next quarterly review goes smoothly. Too smoothly. Someone intervened.

**Outcomes by Roll:**
- Critical success: Everything falls into place. The data, the evidence, the timing. Someone's going to ask how.
- Success: Done. Not clean, not elegant, but done. The colony moves forward.
- Failure: The mission fell apart. The pieces are still useful. Rearranged, they form a different picture.
- Critical failure: Total loss. The situation is worse than before the attempt. And now they know you tried.

**Dialogue During Quest:**
- Joaquin: "I came here to find something. Not thermal cores. Something else. Something personal."
- Player: [Respond / Stay Silent / Leave]
- Joaquin: "The waste processing unit is running cleaner than spec. Nobody upgraded it. HERMES says it optimized itself."

**Reward:** 14 thermal cores, thermal core extraction rights for Section F

### [SEQ:188] [Data Pad] [22:53:02]
============================================================

## DATA PAD: Research Log -- Fatima Dranth
**Found at:** Thalassa Deep | **Tone:** clinical | **Type:** research log

---

Day 77.

Sample degradation: 0.4% per hour. Cause: unknown. Classification: pending.

The readings don't make sense. Not wrong. They make sense, just not in any framework I was trained in. precursor ruins is producing output that the spectrometer interprets as noise. It isn't noise. Noise is random. This has structure. Mathematical structure. The kind that implies a system behind it.

I ran the analysis twice. Both times the software flagged the data as 'instrument error.' The instrument is fine. I calibrated it this morning. The data is accurate. The data is also impossible.

-- Fatima Dranth, Lab 2

---

Day 82.

Filed the anomaly report. Standard form. Ref AR-2693. Dr. Vance reviewed it, handed it back, and told me to rerun the tests. I reran them. Same results. She told me to rerun them again.

I understand now that the form isn't for reporting anomalies. The form is for making anomalies disappear.

Victor from Lab 2 transferred out. No notice. His workstation was cleared by 0600. The samples are still here. Nobody came for them. Nobody came for his things either.

---

Day 86.

Neural activity detected in tissue sample 7-C. Tissue sample 7-C was inorganic.

I've stopped filing reports. I've started keeping this instead. The samples from Thalassa Deep are doing something at night that I can't explain with the equipment I've been given. So I requisitioned better equipment. Request denied. Budget code: INSUFFICIENT AUTHORIZATION.

I brought my personal spectrometer. The readings don't match the Mammona-issue unit. Not slightly off. Fundamentally different. Like the standard equipment is calibrated to miss what I'm finding.

That's not a malfunction. That's a decision someone made.

---

Day 101.

Ash Oduya approached me after shift. Said they saw my after-hours lab access in the logs. I expected a warning. Instead: "I've been seeing the same thing in the Fall of Fortuna. For months. My reports go nowhere too."

We compared data. The correlation is. I don't have a word for it. These aren't coincidences. There's a pattern. The pattern has intent.

I locked the data on a sealed drive. Personal encryption. If the standard equipment is lying to us, I don't trust the standard network either.

---

Day 116.

The specimen measured 0.3 meters at recovery. Current: 0.7 meters. Growth rate: accelerating.

Dr. Oduya didn't show up for shift. Transferred, they said. Same word they used for Victor. Same paperwork. Same empty workstation by morning.

I checked the sealed drive. The data I locked is still there. But there's a new file. I didn't create it. It's a personnel dossier. My personnel dossier. With a field I've never seen before: RETENTION STATUS. The value is PENDING.

---

Day 131.

Something happened last night. I went to check the samples at 0300. They were arranged differently. Not scattered. Arranged. In a pattern I recognized from my own notes. Notes that are on the sealed drive. Notes that nobody has seen.

I don't think I'm studying these samples anymore. I think they're studying me.

-- Fatima Dranth

[This datapad was found face-down on the lab bench. The lab was empty. The samples were gone.]

---

### [SEQ:190] [Quest] [22:53:03]
============================================================

## QUEST: On Record
**Genre:** Moral Dilemma | **Tone:** wrongness / claustrophobia
**Location:** Ashrun | **Faction:** Veil Covenant

**Trigger:**
Isa Venin finds a file in Veil Covenant's local database. It was supposed to be encrypted. It's not. Inside: records of seven colonies. Seven failures. Not accidents. Designed failures. Insurance payouts. Tax write-offs. The colony they're standing in is number eight.

**Setup:**
The clock read 25:17. It stayed there for an hour that felt like three. Isa has the file on a data drive. Small enough to hide. Large enough to end Veil Covenant. Or large enough to end Isa. The file includes projected casualty timelines. For this colony. The timeline is ahead of schedule.

The hab pod seated four. There were six of them. Elbows and knees and recycled breath.

**Key NPC:** Isa Venin (Mining: 9, Willpower: 6) -- their mining skill determines the approach. They motivation: get off Erebus by any means. Legal, illegal, doesn't matter.

**Objectives:**
1. Verify the file. Cross-reference the seven colonies with public records. The losses match. The insurance claims match. The 'unforeseen circumstances' are identical.
2. Decide what to do with the evidence. The comms array can broadcast to the wider network. Veil Covenant can't stop a broadband pulse. But they can trace it.
3. Protect Isa. Once this file moves, Isa becomes a target. Maybe they already are.

**Required Checks:**
- Medical (6+, hard) -- stabilize the wounded before transport
- Negotiation (5+, normal) -- broker a truce before shots are fired
- Research (5+, normal) -- identify the artifact's origin

**If Medical succeeds:** The diagnosis is clear. Treatment is possible. Barely. But possible.
**If Medical fails:** Missed the critical symptom. The window for treatment is closing.
**If Negotiation succeeds:** Terms accepted. Nobody's happy. That means it's fair.
**If Negotiation fails:** Impasse. The conversation ended politely. Nothing was resolved.
**If Research succeeds:** The data breaks open. Not just an answer. A new framework for the question.
**If Research fails:** The data is corrupt. Or the hypothesis is wrong. Three days of work, gone.

**Conditions:**
- Ice fog (visibility 30%, Perception at disadvantage)
- Night shift (reduced visibility, +10 to Stealth)
- Lockdown protocol active (all bulkheads sealed, movement restricted)

**The Choice:**
Give the file to a rival faction. Let them fight it out. Stay out of the crossfire.
OR
Present it directly to Veil Covenant's local representative. Confront them. See what they offer to make this go away. Take their measure.

**Twist:**
Isa planted the file. It's partially real, partially fabricated. Isa has their own agenda. The truth is in there, but so are Isa's lies. And you can't tell which is which.

**Faction Stakes:**
- Veil Covenant wants the evidence destroyed. Compliance: +reputation, -11 thermal cores as 'bonus'
- Cult of the Abyss wants Isa Venin extracted. Compliance: you lose a colonist. They gain an asset.
- The colony needs the resources. Both sides are offering. Both sides are lying about the price.

**Consequences (if Choice A):**
- the medical wing reopened. What's inside changes the colony's understanding of the site.
- Isa Venin's arc shifts from 'suspicious' to 'vindicated.'
- Three colonists file transfer requests. None are approved.

**Consequences (if Choice B):**
- The evidence is destroyed. The questions remain. Nobody asks them out loud.
- Isa Venin's arc shifts from 'suspicious' to 'paranoid.'
- Cult of the Abyss makes contact. They know what happened. They have a proposal.

**Outcomes by Roll:**
- Critical success: Clean resolution. No casualties, no complications. The kind of outcome that makes people suspicious.
- Success: Done. Not clean, not elegant, but done. The colony moves forward.
- Failure: Objective failed, but information gained. The failure teaches more than success would have.
- Critical failure: Objective failed AND new threat introduced. The colony's problems just multiplied.

**Dialogue During Quest:**
- Isa: "If you've got any pull with the roster, move me off the night shift. Please."
- Player: [Respond / Stay Silent / Leave]
- Isa: "I'm not as good at this job as they think. Been faking competence for six months. Nobody's died yet. Yet."

**Reward:** 13 thermal cores, new NPC ally

## DATA PAD: Audio Transcript -- Liesel Vale
**Found at:** Labor Camp Sigma | **Tone:** obsession | **Type:** audio transcript

---

[Recording begins. Timestamp: 18:33. Location: Labor Camp Sigma. Background: wind against hull, gusting.]

The pattern was almost there. One more look. One more hour. One more shift.

Liesel: ...recording. Okay. It's on. This is for the record. Whatever record means on this posting.

---

Liesel: The thing about Labor Camp Sigma. We all know. That's the part nobody talks about. Everyone on this posting knows something is wrong, and not in a way you can fix. In the way that a clock running backward is wrong. The machinery works. The numbers add up. But the direction is wrong.

[Pause: 6 seconds]

---

Rin: Why are you recording this? Liesel, if they find this--

Liesel: I'm past caring. About Mammona, about the contract, about what happens to me. Someone needs to know.

He couldn't stop checking the readings. Every four minutes. The interval was getting shorter.

---

Rin: I found the same thing. In the medical files. Patient records that don't match real people. Treatment protocols for conditions that aren't in any database. And a line item in the budget for 'specimen preparation.' We're not mining here. We've never been mining here.

Liesel: Keep reading. The last page. ... [silence: 14 seconds] ... Yeah. That's the face I made too.

---

Rin: Destroy it. Destroy the recording, destroy the files, and never speak about this again.

Liesel: Tell them what? They know Mammona lied. Tell them what's underneath? We can't leave. The shuttle comes when it comes. We'd just be scared people who can't go anywhere.

[Both speakers begin talking at once. Their words are indistinguishable. The overlap continues for 12 seconds, growing quieter, until both voices stop simultaneously. Not trailing off. Stopping. Mid-word.]

- a NutriLoaf wrapper folded into an origami crane. The folding technique isn't human.

## DATA PAD: Medical Report -- Saskia Yamamoto
**Found at:** Perimeter Outpost Delta | **Tone:** slow_dread | **Type:** medical report

---

**PATIENT:** Margaux Vance
**ATTENDING:** Dr. Saskia Yamamoto
**DATE:** Day 102 of Assignment
**CLASSIFICATION:** Standard

Patient presented with unexplained bruising on the forearms, bilateral. Standard workup ordered. Blood panel, neural scan, toxicology. All results within normal parameters. Prescribed rest cycle extension and monitoring.

Patient cooperative. Affect: appropriate. No immediate concerns.

-- Dr. Saskia Yamamoto

---

**FOLLOW-UP:** Day 106
**CLASSIFICATION:** Standard

Symptoms persisting. Patient reports new development: aversion to processed food. States it 'tastes like a signal'. Blood work flagged by automated system but override applied per standing Mammona medical protocol.

Note: patient's resting heart rate has decreased from 72bpm to 47bpm since initial presentation. Cause unclear. Patient reports feeling 'calmer than I should.'

-- Dr. Saskia Yamamoto

---

**FOLLOW-UP:** Day 118
**CLASSIFICATION:** Restricted

Condensation on the pipes used to drip. Now it ran in a direction. Always the same direction. Toward the bore shaft.

Patient's neural scan shows anomalous activity in regions that should be dormant during waking hours. I've requested a second scanner. Request denied. Reason: 'equipment allocation insufficient for non-critical cases.'

This is not a non-critical case. But I don't have the vocabulary to explain why, because the vocabulary I'd need doesn't exist in the diagnostic manual.

Patient drew a diagram during evaluation. Unprompted. The diagram matches schematics for the Janus AI that are classified above my clearance level. Patient has no access to classified materials. Patient says she 'just knew what it looked like.'

Storing original diagram in personal effects. Not filing with Mammona medical.

-- Dr. Saskia Yamamoto

---

**UPDATE:** Day 128
**CLASSIFICATION:** Restricted / Protocol 7

Patient's condition reclassified under Protocol 7 ('Anomalous Presentation'). I was not informed that Protocol 7 files route directly to MasTema until after I filed.

Patient found in Section E at 0300, standing in front of a sealed door, apparently asleep. No memory of walking there. The door has no handle on the outside. Patient's handprint was on the door. The door is steel. The handprint was warm.

I have requested consultation with a specialist. Request forwarded to MasTema. No response.

-- Dr. Saskia Yamamoto

---

**NOTE:** Day 144
**CLASSIFICATION:** Personal / Not Filed

I'm no longer confident this is a medical issue. I'm no longer confident in the word 'issue.' Patient is aware of things. Things she shouldn't be aware of. She knew about the supply ship delay before comms received the update. If this is a disease, it's improving her. That's not how disease works. That's not how anything works.

Unless the improvement is the disease. Unless what I'm calling improvement is something else wearing a familiar shape.

I don't know anymore. I'm filing this report because filing reports is what I do. I don't know what else to do.

-- Dr. Saskia Yamamoto

---

**ADDENDUM** (handwritten, different hand):

Dr. Yamamoto: your patient is fine. Your patient has always been fine. Your patient is the only person on this posting who is fine.

The question you should be asking isn't 'what's wrong with Margaux?' The question is 'why isn't it happening to everyone?'

Check your own bloodwork, Doctor. Then check it again in a week.

-- [unsigned]

[This addendum was found on a separate data pad, placed inside Dr. Yamamoto's medical kit. Dr. Yamamoto has no record of receiving it.]

### [SEQ:197] [Data Pad] [22:53:03]
============================================================

## DATA PAD: Research Log -- Ezekiel Deepwell
**Found at:** The Gutter's Pearl | **Tone:** the_uncanny | **Type:** research log

---

Day 31.

The food tasted exactly like the food from home. Exactly. Down to a spice that shouldn't exist here.

Something is wrong with the control group. The control group should be the one thing that's not wrong. That's what 'control' means. The baseline samples from The Gutter's Pearl are changing at the same rate as the experimental ones. No stimulus. No exposure. Sealed containers, inert atmosphere, stable temperature.

They're changing anyway. And they're changing in the same direction as Skinwalkers. Like there's a signal I can't see. Like the experiment is running itself.

-- Ezekiel Deepwell, Lab 3

---

Day 34.

Filed the anomaly report. Standard form. Ref AR-4554. Dr. Dvorak reviewed it, handed it back, and told me to rerun the tests. I reran them. Same results. He told me to rerun them again.

I understand now that the form isn't for reporting anomalies. The form is for making anomalies disappear.

Soren from Lab 2 transferred out. No notice. His workstation was cleared by 0600. The samples are still here. Nobody came for them. Nobody came for his things either.

---

Day 43.

They walked past their own reflection. It was a half-second slow.

I've stopped filing reports. I've started keeping this instead. The samples from The Gutter's Pearl are doing something at night that I can't explain with the equipment I've been given. So I requisitioned better equipment. Request denied. Budget code: INSUFFICIENT AUTHORIZATION.

I brought my personal spectrometer. The readings don't match the Mammona-issue unit. Not slightly off. Fundamentally different. Like the standard equipment is calibrated to miss what I'm finding.

That's not a malfunction. That's a decision someone made.

---

Day 53.

Kwame Petrov approached me after shift. Said he saw my after-hours lab access in the logs. I expected a warning. Instead: "I've been seeing the same thing in the Frequency. For months. My reports go nowhere too."

We compared data. The correlation is. I don't have a word for it. These aren't coincidences. There's a pattern. The pattern has intent.

I locked the data on a sealed drive. Personal encryption. If the standard equipment is lying to us, I don't trust the standard network either.

---

Day 67.

The new transfer smiled. Too wide. The muscles in their face didn't quite coordinate.

Dr. Petrov didn't show up for shift. Transferred, they said. Same word they used for Soren. Same paperwork. Same empty workstation by morning.

I checked the sealed drive. The data I locked is still there. But there's a new file. I didn't create it. It's a personnel dossier. My personnel dossier. With a field I've never seen before: RETENTION STATUS. The value is PENDING.

---

Day 73.

Check cabinet 10. The real readings are taped to the back panel. Compare them to what's in the system. Then decide what kind of person you want to be.

-- Ezekiel Deepwell

[No further entries. The lab was reassigned on Day 74.]

---

**Era:** present | **Tone:** desperate

**ATTENDING:** Dr. Kenji Sato
**DATE:** Day 153 of Assignment
**CLASSIFICATION:** Standard

Patient presented with a persistent low-grade fever with no identifiable pathogen. Standard workup ordered. Blood panel, neural scan, toxicology. All results within normal parameters. Prescribed rest cycle extension and monitoring.

Patient cooperative. Affect: appropriate. No immediate concerns.

-- Dr. Kenji Sato

---

**FOLLOW-UP:** Day 159
**CLASSIFICATION:** Standard

Symptoms persisting. Patient reports new development: awareness of other colonists' locations without visual confirmation. Administered standard anxiolytic. Patient reported no effect after 48 hours.

Note: patient's resting heart rate has decreased from 72bpm to 47bpm since initial presentation. Cause unclear. Patient reports feeling 'calmer than I should.'

-- Dr. Kenji Sato

---

**FOLLOW-UP:** Day 166
**CLASSIFICATION:** Restricted

His hands did the work. The rest of him was somewhere else. Somewhere horizontal.

Patient's neural scan shows anomalous activity in regions that should be dormant during waking hours. I've requested a second scanner. Request denied. Reason: 'equipment allocation insufficient for non-critical cases.'

This is not a non-critical case. But I don't have the vocabulary to explain why, because the vocabulary I'd need doesn't exist in the diagnostic manual.

Patient drew a diagram during evaluation. Unprompted. The diagram matches schematics for Eldritch Nodes that are classified above my clearance level. Patient has no access to classified materials. Patient says she 'just knew what it looked like.'

Storing original diagram in personal effects. Not filing with Mammona medical.

-- Dr. Kenji Sato

---

**UPDATE:** Day 177
**CLASSIFICATION:** Restricted / Protocol 7

Patient's condition reclassified under Protocol 7 ('Anomalous Presentation'). I was not informed that Protocol 7 files route directly to MasTema until after I filed.

Patient found in Section D at 0300, standing in front of a sealed door, apparently asleep. No memory of walking there. The door has no handle on the outside. Patient's handprint was on the door. The door is steel. The handprint was warm.

I have requested consultation with a specialist. Request forwarded to MasTema. No response.

-- Dr. Kenji Sato

---

**NOTE:** Day 190
**CLASSIFICATION:** Personal / Not Filed

I'm no longer confident this is a medical issue. I'm no longer confident in the word 'issue.' Patient is drawing. Constantly. The same structures. From angles that don't exist in three-dimensional space. If this is a disease, it's improving her. That's not how disease works. That's not how anything works.

Unless the improvement is the disease. Unless what I'm calling improvement is something else wearing a familiar shape.

I don't know anymore. I'm filing this report because filing reports is what I do. I don't know what else to do.

-- Dr. Kenji Sato

---

**ADDENDUM** (handwritten, different hand):

Doctor Sato's notes are thorough and accurate. The observations are described. What they mean is not.

What it means is that Esperanza Norris is no longer the patient. Esperanza Norris is the vector. The patient is everyone else.

Recommend immediate

### [SEQ:203] [Quest] [22:53:04]
============================================================

## QUEST: Retrieval
**Genre:** Expedition | **Tone:** dissociation / identity_erosion
**Location:** Thalassa Deep | **Faction:** Veilbreakers

**Trigger:**
The survey team went out three days ago. They found something in the ruins. Something valuable. Then comms went dead. Odessa Rimgate picks up a final transmission: coordinates, a single word, 'hurry,' and the sound of something large moving through stone.

**Setup:**
Sounds came from very far away. Her own voice was the farthest. The survey team's last known position is a precursor site twelve kilometers south. The trail is easy to follow. Their vehicle tracks cut clear lines in the ice. Too easy. Halfway there, Odessa notices the tracks are paralleled by something else. Footprints. Barefoot. In negative forty. Walking the same direction.

They asked her to describe her childhood. She started twice. Different details each time.

**Key NPC:** Odessa Rimgate (Mining: 10, Willpower: 6) -- her mining skill determines the approach. She motivation: master the bore shafts. Know them better than anyone alive. Own the knowledge that keeps the colony running.

**Objectives:**
1. Reach the survey site. The vehicle is there. Engine cold. Doors open. Equipment scattered. No bodies.
2. Find the team. The footprints, human and otherwise, lead into the precursor structure. The structure is larger than the survey map indicated.
3. Retrieve what the team found. It's in the structure. So is whatever took them. Both are between you and the exit.

**Required Checks:**
- Mining (4+, easy) -- drill through the sealed bulkhead
- Combat (8+, extreme) -- defend the reactor during the breach
- Perception (4+, easy) -- spot the tripwire before it's too late

**If Mining succeeds:** The passage opens. Behind it: a room that shouldn't exist. Pre-colony construction.
**If Mining fails:** The collapse spreads. The passage is gone. But the sound from the other side continues.
**If Combat succeeds:** Controlled violence. The threat is down. The corridor is clear. For now.
**If Combat fails:** The advantage shifted. Someone's bleeding. The situation deteriorated.
**If Perception succeeds:** There it is. The detail everyone missed. It changes the equation.
**If Perception fails:** Looked right at it. Didn't see it. The brain filtered it out as normal.

**Conditions:**
- Ice fog (visibility 30%, Perception at disadvantage)
- Night shift (reduced visibility, +10 to Stealth)
- HERMES in maintenance mode (no surveillance for 45 minutes)

**The Choice:**
Rescue the team. They might be alive. Three days in a precursor ruin with something hunting them. Alive is optimistic. But possible.
OR
Retrieve the artifact and leave. The artifact is why they were sent. Cold calculus. Mammona's favorite kind.

**Twist:**
The artifact the team found isn't an object. It's information. Carved into the walls: a complete map of every precursor site on Erebus. There are hundreds. And they're connected. Underground. To something central.

**Faction Stakes:**
- Veilbreakers wants the data encrypted and shipped off-planet. Compliance: colony loses leverage but gains credits
- The Ashen Circuit wants the site destroyed. Compliance: the evidence is gone. So is whatever else was down there.
- The colonists don't know about this yet. When they find out, morale takes the hit regardless of outcome.

**Consequences (if Choice A):**
- The evidence is preserved. It's leverage now. The question is who holds it.
- Odessa Rimgate's arc shifts from 'suspicious' to 'vindicated.'
- Veilbreakers sends a follow-up team. The team asks questions nobody wants answered.

**Consequences (if Choice B):**
- Section D stays sealed. The sound from inside doesn't stop.
- Odessa Rimgate's arc shifts from 'suspicious' to 'paranoid.'
- The next quarterly review goes smoothly. Too smoothly. Someone intervened.

**Outcomes by Roll:**
- Critical success: Clean resolution. No casualties, no complications. The kind of outcome that makes people suspicious.
- Success: Primary objective achieved, secondary compromised. The cost was acceptable. Barely.
- Failure: Didn't get what you came for. Got something else. It might be worse.
- Critical failure: Objective failed AND new threat introduced. The colony's problems just multiplied.

**Dialogue During Quest:**
- Odessa: "Remember me. If I don't come back, remember me. That's all I'm asking."
- Player: [Respond / Stay Silent / Leave]
- Odessa: "Keep your radio on. Keep your head down."

**Reward:** 10 thermal cores, a key to a room that isn't on any map

### [SEQ:205] [History Event] [22:53:04]
============================================================

## HISTORY: Supply Manifest Discrepancy
**Era:** fortuna | **Tone:** survival_horror

Two medkits for seventeen people. The math was simple. The choices weren't.

During construction of the colony in 2586, the foundation team discovered a chamber 75 meters below grade. The chamber was empty except for 15 identical marks on the walls. The marks match a Mammona corporate logo that wasn't designed until 2590.

**Significance:** This pattern predates human presence on the planet. It continued through human presence on the planet. It's continuing now.

**Mechanical Impact:**
- Colony morale: -3 for one week (the news spreads)
- Section C: sealed (inaccessible until quest completes)
- NPC Ingrid Reznik: arc shifts to 'suspicious'
- HERMES reclassifies the location. The new classification is above colony clearance.

**Evidence:**
- Maintenance log #1094 (references an equipment requisition for items that don't exist)
- Tool marks on the sealed door. Someone tried to open it. From the inside.
- A colonist's journal entry that stops mid-sentence on the day it happened
- HERMES flagged the event internally, then removed the flag. The removal is logged. The original flag is not.

**Who Knows:**
- **Charles Orosco:** was on shift when it happened. Says nothing unusual occurred. Their hands shake when they say it.
- **Kira Nakamura:** heard about it secondhand. Has theories. The theories are wrong but close.
- **Thea Rathmore:** has no connection to the event. But they've been dreaming about it. Accurately.

**Aftermath:**
- Shift schedules were restructured. The restructuring moved three people away from the affected area. No reason given.
- Fortune Arms & Munitions made inquiries. The inquiries were careful. Indirect. The kind of careful that means they already know.
- Someone started leaving offerings near the site. Small things. Food, water, a folded note. Nobody claims responsibility.

**HERMES Analysis:**
HERMES generated a 14-page analysis. The analysis was compressed to a single paragraph for the colony briefing. The paragraph says: 'No anomalies detected.' The 58 pages say otherwise.

**Related Incidents:**
A similar event was recorded at Port Meridian in 2583. The similarities were noted by one analyst. The analyst was reassigned.

**Investigation Check:**
- Deception (6+, hard) -- dig deeper into what happened
- **If successful:** the full picture emerges. The event connects to the Bloom. The connection is undeniable.
- **If failed:** nothing. Which, on a Mammona posting, means someone made the evidence into nothing. Absence with fingerprints.

### [SEQ:206] [Data Pad] [22:53:04]
============================================================

## DATA PAD: Maintenance Log -- Sasha Kowalski
**Found at:** Voidbloom Cavern | **Tone:** bitter_hope | **Type:** maintenance log

---

**MAINTENANCE LOG -- Power Conduit F-9**
**Tech:** Sasha Kowalski (SK-337)
**Date:** Day 56

Routine inspection. All parameters within spec. Filter replacement completed. Calibration nominal. Estimated next service: Day 86.

Notes: None. Clean run.

-- SK-337

---

**Date:** Day 64

Unscheduled check. Night shift reported a vibration in the walls near the assembly. Inspected. Couldn't reproduce. All readings nominal at time of inspection.

Action: monitoring. Will revisit next scheduled maintenance.

-- SK-337

---

**Date:** Day 82

The signal was weak. It could be a ship. It could be nothing. They suited up anyway.

Follow-up on previous entry. The condensation is back. Tested the liquid. It's not condensation. Chemical analysis pending but preliminary taste test (yes, I know) suggests organic origin.

Submitted work order for diagnostic overhaul. Status: queued. Estimated wait: 5 weeks.

Something isn't right. I don't have data to support that statement. After 17 years of fixing machines, you develop a feeling in your hands. The feeling says something isn't right.

-- SK-337

---

**Date:** Day 90

Diagnostic overhaul completed. 5 hours of testing. Every component individually verified. Every sensor calibrated. Every connection checked.

Result: the system is operating perfectly. Better than perfectly. Efficiency is up 9% from installation baseline. That shouldn't be possible on equipment this age with this service history.

But the sound is still there. And now I can hear it from the corridor. And now it has a rhythm. And the rhythm matches the drill cycle at Deep Bore Alpha. Power Conduit F-9 has no connection to the drill. No shared power bus, no shared conduit, no shared anything. There's no mechanical path for that vibration to travel. But it's here.

I'm filing this under 'resolved, nominal' because that's what the data says. The data is wrong. I don't know how to file that.

-- SK-337

---

**Date:** Day 111

He kept the letter of transfer in his pocket. Read it every night. The date was two years old.

The system has started performing maintenance on itself. I watched it. Through the inspection port. Components moving. Adjusting. Tightening connections I'd left loose on purpose, as test markers. Nobody else was in the section.

Machines don't do that. This isn't a machine anymore. I can't name what it's become.

I'm going to close this log and start a new one. The new one will say everything is fine.

-- SK-337

[No further entries in this log. Subsequent maintenance logs for Power Conduit F-9 are filed by a different technician. They describe the system as 'nominal.']

### [SEQ:212] [History Event] [22:53:05]
============================================================

## HISTORY: Perimeter Breach Pattern
**Era:** fortuna | **Tone:** clinical

Neural activity detected in tissue sample 7-C. Tissue sample 7-C was inorganic.

In 2585, The Ashen Circuit conducted an unscheduled survey of Rusted War Field. The team spent 12 weeks on site. The report they filed was 321 pages long. The redacted version is 5 pages.

**Significance:** The event was classified. The classification level is higher than any individual on the posting had access to. Someone else is watching.

**Mechanical Impact:**
- Colony morale: -10 for one week (the news spreads)
- the lower levels: sealed (inaccessible until quest completes)
- NPC Kenji MacReady: arc shifts to 'paranoid'
- The Ashen Circuit dispatches an 'observer.' The observer asks no questions. Takes notes.

**Evidence:**
- Maintenance log #1087 (references nothing. The entry for that date is blank. Every other entry is filled.)
- A structural crack in the floor of Hab 2 that follows no natural fault line
- A data drive hidden in the wall panel of Bunk 11. Encrypted. Personal key.
- HERMES flagged the event internally, then removed the flag. The removal is logged. The original flag is not.

**Who Knows:**
- **Charles Orosco:** filed a report afterward. The report was rejected. They filed it again. Rejected again.
- **Dorian Liu:** has been asking questions. The questions are making people uncomfortable.
- **Minerva Petrov:** knows nothing. Arrived after. But found something in their quarters that predates their arrival.

**Aftermath:**
- The supply manifest format changed. The new format has a field labeled 'ANOMALY FLAG.' It is always set to NO.
- A sealed communication was sent to MasTema. Response: 'Acknowledged.' No follow-up. No action. Just acknowledgment.
- Someone started leaving offerings near the site. Small things. Food, water, a folded note. Nobody claims responsibility.

**HERMES Analysis:**
HERMES's response to queries about this event changed on Day 66. Before: detailed, factual, cooperative. After: 'Please direct inquiries to your site manager.' The site manager was not informed of this change.

**Related Incidents:**
Colony Ashford Station reported identical thermal readings 7 days before their evacuation. The readings were dismissed as calibration error.

**Investigation Check:**
- Research (6+, hard) -- dig deeper into what happened
- **If successful:** the pattern becomes visible. This happened before. Under different names. Same outcome.
- **If failed:** dead end. But the dead end is instructive. Someone put a wall exactly where you needed a door.

### [SEQ:225] [History Event] [22:53:06]
============================================================

## HISTORY: Foundation Discovery
**Era:** corporate | **Tone:** desperate

The radio crackled. Behind the static, something that might have been a voice. Or a heartbeat.

A colonist named Isaac Jokinen vanished from the roster 11 months before your crew arrived. No transfer order. No death certificate. Personal effects are still in Hab 6, untouched. Nobody reassigned the bunk.

**Significance:** The previous crew knew something. The question is whether their silence was chosen or enforced.

**Mechanical Impact:**
- Colony morale: -10 for until resolved (the news spreads)
- the lower levels: sealed (inaccessible until quest completes)
- NPC Solene da Silva: arc shifts to 'paranoid'
- OmniCorp Shipping dispatches an 'observer.' The observer asks no questions. Takes notes.

**Evidence:**
- Maintenance log #5212 (references a 'routine personnel transfer' on the same date)
- Tool marks on the sealed door. Someone tried to open it. From the inside.
- A data drive hidden in the wall panel of Bunk 19. Encrypted. Personal key.
- HERMES flagged the event internally, then removed the flag. The removal is logged. The original flag is not.

**Who Knows:**
- **Rolf Schmidt:** was on shift when it happened. Says nothing unusual occurred. Their hands shake when they say it.
- **Noor Oduya:** has been asking questions. The questions are making people uncomfortable.
- **Linnea Khoury:** has no connection to the event. But they've been dreaming about it. Accurately.

**Aftermath:**
- Shift schedules were restructured. The restructuring moved three people away from the affected area. No reason given.
- StarByte Vends made inquiries. The inquiries were careful. Indirect. The kind of careful that means they already know.
- Three colonists requested bunk transfers away from the affected area. Two were approved. The third withdrew the request without explanation.

**HERMES Analysis:**
HERMES has cross-referenced this event with 4 similar incidents across 3 postings. The correlation is strong. HERMES has not shared this correlation with colony staff. When queried: 'Insufficient clearance.'

**Related Incidents:**
Three postings. Three events. Three sealed reports. The reports use the same classification code. The code isn't in any manual.

**Investigation Check:**
- Deception (6+, hard) -- dig deeper into what happened
- **If successful:** the missing piece falls into place. Not an accident. Not an anomaly. A sequence.
- **If failed:** the investigation alerts someone. Within hours, the remaining evidence begins to disappear.
